  (114 baseline lines).

The owning layer is Hyperreal's query-local radical arithmetic and its shared-root
sign/decline adapter. P1–P6, P10 and P19 govern exact selected roots, conservative
recognition, proof reuse, resource/failure distinctions and downstream predicates.
Inputs include rational leaves, ordered dependent/independent square-root extensions,
raw arithmetic DAGs, exact rational-angle sine leaves and invalid-domain expressions.
The missing witness was complete private/helper/test Rustdoc and accurate descriptions
of guard scope, basis identity and cached outcomes. On the baseline, all three
raw-graph eighth-angle tests and five Real radical tests passed before editing.

All 46 authored declarations/fields/variants now have Rustdoc. The audit records:

- RadicalElement is a boxed coefficient tree, not a shared DAG. Its generator
  indices refer to one RadicalTower; indices from separate towers are not identities.
  Derived equality compares presentation with exact rational leaf equality, not all
  equivalent scalar expressions. Structural zero requires every leaf zero; dependent
  root relations can prove additional zeros. Clone preserves values but duplicates
  boxed coefficient structure. Root relations are positive and ordered by dependency.
- Addition aligns levels and join removes only structurally unused high parts.
  Multiplication applies the exact square relation. Sign compares opposed terms by
  squared magnitudes and remains valid for dependent generators. Conjugate inversion
  can nevertheless decline a nonzero value with zero norm. The old zero-norm comment
  was corrected: zero norm can also arise from a zero value, and does not by itself
  prove that the root generator is dependent.
- Guard names do not constitute a total-work budget. The 256-node threshold counts
  completed memo entries, excluding pending depth and separate helper traversal;
  the ten-generator threshold applies after rational-root/tree-reuse attempts.
  The 256-term measure counts all rational leaves, including zeros. The 4096-bit
  measure takes the maximum canonical numerator-plus-denominator size of any leaf,
  not their sum. Rational accessors may canonicalize and cache fractions while
  measuring them. Exact-rational traversal shortcuts bypass element checks.
- Products and completed ordinary graph nodes apply size guards after construction.
  Addition, sign differences and generator relations are not uniformly guarded
  intermediates, and there is no cumulative work/allocation/cancellation bound.
  Offsets build a separate power-of-two factor before scaling, so their shift guard
  does not cancel powers already in a child as the quadratic coefficient path does.
  These are current implementation limits, not changes to the target resource contract.
- Rational-root recognition reads canonical magnitudes but assumes nonnegative input.
  Its shared partial square extractor can decline beyond its recognition envelope;
  decline is not a nonsquare proof. Positive radicands first try that shortcut, then
  exactly equal existing trees, then a new generator. No complete basis minimization
  or independence proof is required for the sign argument.
- PrescaledSin admits recognized pi/8 and 3*pi/8 arguments via their positive
  half-angle roots, retaining the source sine nodes. The separate pi-multiple
  recognizer owns additional traversal limits. A local radical basis is discarded
  after every query; successful signs, but not that basis, are retained. Calling
  this method again after success rebuilds the basis. Every decline is memoized
  without a reason or caller budget/policy key; other sign-query paths remain usable.
  Unsupported syntax, domain failure, dependent-root inversion and guard decline
  remain combined in Option, not typed exhaustion or universal undecidability.
- Raw test helpers bypass constructor simplification and start with invalid facts.
  The four half-angle identities have twelve signed residual cases, each queried
  twice without a numeric root cache; sine tags remain intact. The rejection test
  covers four unsupported arguments and inverse zero, with no negative-radicand
  witness. The test named full_hull_determinant evaluates a supplied factored scalar
  expression and does not call a hull/four-point determinant implementation.

kernel. A compiled public consumer exercised the four eighth-angle identities,
twelve signed residual cases and cloned retries, dependent-root cancellation and
repeated pi decline. All passed against the rebuilt library.

Baseline: 82b8ce6eadb1e6687f8950df1470b0188001cc05. Read all 882 baseline lines

inline stack, local continuation enum, every query branch and existing examples.
The owner is Hyperreal's computable evaluation/query layer. P1, P3–P6, P9–P10 and
P19 govern approximation enclosures, conservative facts, monotone caches, distinct
resource controls, failure/certainty reporting, dispatch order and retained proof
consumption. The input domain is valid exact expression graphs with attached or

The missing witness was complete private stack/field/local-enum Rustdoc plus accurate

cancellation. Five linear-demand and four absolute-comparison tests passed on the

Equal versus exact order and the debug overflow at the minimum absolute tolerance
before editing. Its initial use of a private shift helper was replaced with the
public exact-ratio constructor; no repository implementation changed for the probe.

All 39 authored declarations/fields/variants now have documentation:

- InlineStack is a LIFO with an occupied inline prefix and later vector entries;
  spill is unbounded and N=0 is valid. Values move rather than clone. The local
  continuation enum documents each parent/child precision and both tuple fields
  of every variant. Addition scheduling may reverse child evaluation order while
  retaining the same two guard bits and exact sum.
- approx returns a scaled integer with the ordinary one-unit enclosure guarantee
  on valid completed evaluation, not a canonical/correctly-rounded conversion.
  Both executable examples were simplified without weakening their assertions.
  near_integer makes one outer precision -2 request and rounds its result divided
  by four; the 3/4 combined error proves adjacency. One request is not a total-work
  bound, and incomplete interrupted evaluation has no adjacency guarantee.
- approx_signal uses the explicit signal in place of the wrapper attachment.
  Exact leaves, shared-constant caches, node caches and retained quadratic towers
  precede kernels. Negate/Add/Offset use explicit stacks; other kernels can recurse.
  Publication suppresses interrupted results and retains stronger/finer evidence,
  but the returned BigInt has no cancellation receipt. An asserted signal may
  coexist with a completed exact/cache shortcut or an incomplete kernel result.
  Precision-dependent integer storage also depends on the input magnitude; the
  old comment bounding limb count solely by requested precision was corrected.
- immediate_sign only reads retained root facts. structural_facts and zero_status
  can perform structural analysis and cache updates without requesting new numeric
  refinement. Sign, unsigned nonzero, exact-rational availability and qualified
  magnitude remain distinct; missing rational evidence is not irrationality proof.
- sign_until preserves its exact-sign/cache/bound/filter/refinement order and
  deferred algebraic zero-target check. Its floor constrains outer requests, not
  finer reused evidence or child guard bits. None remains unresolved; interruption
  has no separate receipt and the signal is not polled at every return. No precision
  parameter is a cumulative work/memory limit.
- Exact comparison's default tolerance floor is -4096. The explicit-floor path
  preserves structural/shared-perturbation/rational/sign/magnitude proofs before
  lowering comparison tolerances. It never converts unresolved tolerance Equal
  into an exact equality certificate. Exact leaf comparisons borrow wrappers but
  may still allocate rational arithmetic temporaries; the old allocation-free
  comment was narrowed to that actual behavior.
- compare_absolute compares signed values. Exact shortcuts may separate arbitrarily
  close inputs while shared-perturbation tolerance can deliberately return Equal.
  The numerical fallback uses tolerance-1 and a one-integer-unit separation test;
  it is not a uniform approximate-equivalence relation. Derived i32 exponents are
  not uniformly checked. The public debug probe catches specifically "attempt to
  subtract with overflow" for pi versus e at i32::MIN tolerance. This is an existing
  implementation gap, not a typed failure or an intentional narrowed target domain.
- known_msd translates the cached integer's leading bit; it is not a new exact
  binade proof near a boundary and can panic for a missing/unrepresentable cache.
  msd distinguishes exact structural bounds from approximation-based estimates,
  but its None combines known zero and unresolved magnitude. iter_msd_stop always
  starts at zero and still invokes msd(p) after a stop/floor break. iter_msd uses
  STOP_PRECISION for unresolved/zero as well as a possible exponent, so consumers
  must not treat that plain integer as an independent nonzero certificate.

  distinguishes absent, unresolved and certified sign, with Unknown eligible for
  later strengthening. These enum values do not validate their own source identity.
- BoundInfo separates exact zero/nonzero/sign claims from exact binades and inexact
  planning hints. Missing exponents, including overflow, do not prove zero. Inexact
  hints can drift arbitrarily under composition and cannot justify error-sensitive
  precision. Derived equality compares metadata, not represented real values.
- Each transform describes its retained and lost evidence: checked exponent mapping,
  sign negation, reciprocal estimate 1-e, one-stage square estimate 2e, exact positive
  root binade floor(e/2), product exponent sum, and exact-binade sign dominance for
  opposite-sign sums. Zero annihilation requires already-valid operand domains.
  Reciprocal metadata passes Zero through and root metadata returns Unknown for
  negative/unsigned inputs; neither helper is a numeric-domain admission API.
- Projections distinguish None from Some(None), and preserve the exactness flag when
  exporting a present magnitude. The ghost specifications describe the same metadata
  rules; comments do not establish or extend a Verus proof.
- SharedConstant::bound_info supplies exact binades, not merely coarse estimates.
  SharedConstant::interval supplies fixed strict rational endpoints to both
  constant/rational sign checks and native polynomial separation. The earlier
  comment limiting this to one consumer was corrected. The shared numerical cache
  remains process-wide, separate from per-node facts, and not bounded in bytes by
  its fixed slot count.
- Signal shares a cooperative Boolean flag. should_stop is only a relaxed poll:
  it neither publishes unrelated memory nor guarantees completed cancellation,
  response latency or a valid interrupted result. Callers own those obligations.
- Sign-cache tests enumerate ninety packed-metadata combinations, force one stale
  reader/publication interleaving for each sign, and reuse a structurally proved
  sqrt(2)-1 sign without a numerical cache. They do not claim exhaustive schedules.
- Planning tests distinguish finite expanded MPFR enclosures from correctly rounded
  integers or universal exact equality. The arbitrary-hint logarithm fixture has
  sixteen input/hint combinations and warm precision reuse. Long sum/product/root
  cases use independent compact formulas; the eight reciprocal cases rationalize
  the reference formula to avoid its source cancellation. The symbolic complementary
  parameter test exercises ln/exp consumption and a narrow residual interval, not
  a Jacobi evaluation or an independent symbolic identity proof. Tolerance Equal
  remains distinct from the exact order for the small perturbation cases.

## Hyperreal exponential relations and atom-comparison reuse (2026-11-27)

Baseline: 8f13e57af94f8060ee96160e650d273d5550015e. Whole-file review of
computable/node/exp_relation.rs (249 baseline lines), exp_relation_reuse.rs (82),
exp_relation_tests.rs (308) and exp_relation_reuse_tests.rs (154): 793 baseline
lines. The owning layer is Hyperreal exact structural sign recognition and its
thread-local comparison accelerator. Relevant properties are P1–P6, P10 and P19:
exact logarithmic identities, retained node identity, monotone cache evidence,
resource distinctions and replay. Missing witnesses were private Rustdoc on the
proof form, all fields/variants/helpers, TLS state and regression tests. All
eighteen owning tests passed on the baseline before editing.

The reviewed documentation now distinguishes:

- The exact relation is a rational remainder plus weighted opaque real terms,
  a distinguished ln(2) atom, and logarithms of selected positive bases. Sign
  transfers by strict monotonicity of log only after all atoms cancel. This
  does not rewrite graphs or numerically evaluate them. Native mode assumes
  opaque arguments denote valid reals; import mode admits a narrower defined
  grammar and may decline valid or even identical expressions.
- Limits count 128 linear/logarithm entries, sixteen live combined atom slots
  and 1024 bits per checked canonical numerator or denominator. The bit guard
  uses the maximum, not their sum, and access may normalize a rational first.
  Atom comparisons and some temporary arithmetic are outside the visit counter.
  There is no total-work, allocation or cancellation limit supplied by this form.
- Updates are not transactional: a failed charge remains consumed and some
  coefficient merges or traversals partially change the form before declining.
  Callers discard the failed accumulator. None combines grammar, unresolved
  atoms and guard failures without a typed reason; the Boolean test helper's
  false result also combines unresolved and proved-nonzero outcomes.
- Positive rational log atoms compare exact values without general multiplicative
  factorization. Binary powers use ln(2); products, roots, squares and inverses
  transport coefficients only through recognized positive bases. Squaring alone
  does not admit a negative/unknown base. Import mode checks opaque definedness
  before discarding a zero coefficient. Native scalar-product recognition keeps
  its left-first leaf test and the original recursive traversal/removal order.
- The sixteen-slot direct-mapped cache checks both complete node addresses and
  retains weak keys to prevent address reuse. It retains neither live payloads
  nor child graphs after their owners disappear, but weak keys can retain allocation
  storage. Pair ordering gives symmetric lookup; pointer identity bypasses storage.
  A stored false is a structural-recognizer non-match, including unsupported tag
  pairs, rather than proof that represented reals differ. Hash collisions do not
  establish equality. Borrow conflicts or unavailable TLS use the uncached path,
  and no borrow is held while traversing. Cached fields are ignored by that
  recognizer, so refinement cannot invalidate these immutable-shape results.
- The 512-case fixed-seed generator tracks coefficients with independent num
  BigRational arithmetic; it is a finite recipe corpus. Thirty signed dyadic
  cases cover nonzero remainder signs and subtraction order. The 2^-1024 case
  recovers from cached Unknown through finer approximation, not increased
  structural limits. Hot-cache snapshots, retained root tags and same-process
  replay/byte-stability assertions are described separately.
- Cache fixtures cover 512 pairs across three passes, weak-key release at reset
  and worker exit, a forced borrow conflict, and refinement of one valid operand.
  Weak counts do not measure comparator invocations, cache-hit rate or bytes.
  Deep PrescaledSin chains are syntax fixtures that may violate reduced-kernel
  ranges and are not numerically evaluated. The 27 deep relation cases test
  symbolic outcomes, not their numerical domain admission or performance.
- The import-mode invalid-operand cases call the recognizer directly, rather
  than deserializing. The root/product fixture has no inverse case despite its
  name. Tests claiming decline do not establish typed exhaustion or minimal
  recognition thresholds, and no fixture was weakened to change that outcome.

## Hyperreal retained logarithms, Jacobi relations and shared quotients (2026-11-27)

Baseline: 631e08c8f7d2e9f74f265c359ec5249b4831dfbc. Whole-file review of
computable/node/log_argument.rs (80 baseline lines), shared_square_quotient.rs (98),
shared_square_quotient_tests.rs (226), jacobi.rs (103), jacobi_tests.rs (73) and
log_rational_range_tests.rs (121), totaling 701 baseline lines. The owning layer

proof reuse, resource distinctions and retained cancellation controls. Missing

functions and the regression modules/oracles. Ten owning tests passed before edits.

All 29 authored declarations have documentation:

- retained_log_argument recovers exp(self) through a restricted logarithm grammar
  used by Jacobi complement consumers. It requires positive-domain evidence for
  ln(1+r), including a cached residual lower bound strictly greater than -1 when
  direct sign recognition declines. The cached route bounds the absolute stored
  precision exponent by 4096 and requests no new digits. Success publishes a
  positive sign on the recovered expression for subsequent use.
- The shared u8 visit counter is consumed before the entry signal poll; there is
  another poll before return. Failure does not roll back visits or facts strengthened
  by subqueries. None combines invalid/unproved domain, unknown syntax, size/visit
  guards and cancellation. Binary exponent limits, integer-power limits and the
  4096-bit rational guard do not bound all constructor work or temporary storage.
  In particular, binary-scaled log shifts can allocate before the result-size check.
  Even zero integer powers first recover a valid positive child argument.
- Shared reciprocal cancellation requires one retained node allocation and an
  immediate nonzero sign. It removes the whole graph, so it checks descendant
  handles under a 32-pop budget, counting repeated shared visits. All signals
  must have identical Arc identities; their Boolean values are not compared.
  Square quotient cancellation instead retains the original node/descendants
  and reconciles five wrapper handles. Both shortcuts carry compatible asserted
  flags without polling them; neither is a numerical equality solver or a typed
  resource-exhaustion API.
- Jacobi payloads store an amplitude phi and ln(c), with c>0 and parameter m=1-c.
  Components denote sin(phi), cos(phi) and the positive square root of
  cos(phi)^2+c*sin(phi)^2. The constructor does not invert the elliptic integral
  or validate arbitrary child graphs. Its previous broad imported-payload comment
  is now qualified by defined-real input preconditions. The dn zero-log shortcut
  and square-sum helper describe their actual outer-signal priority, without
  claiming exhaustive reconciliation of discarded descendant controls.
- Square extraction limits path depth and follows the left product spine first;
  it does not bound total sibling visits or nested constructor/comparison work.
  Sum recognition requires matching amplitude and parameter shapes, reconstructs
  c before testing guards, then applies the four weighted identities:
  sn²+cn²=1, c*sn²+cn²=dn², (1-c)*sn²+dn²=1, and (c-1)*cn²+dn²=c.
  Coefficient matching first uses structural recognition, then a bounded ring
  zero proof. A false match is not an inequality certificate. Dispatch and guard
  order remain unchanged.
- Shared-quotient fixtures distinguish structural equality from allocation
  identity, exercise both shapes/orders/signs, preserve cache snapshots, inspect
  all five signal positions and consume resumed outputs after clearing a flag.
  Their inspection-limit case does not establish a minimal threshold or latency.
- Log recovery tests check nine independent rational results, six shared logarithms,
  a square-root relation, zero visits, selected invalid/unrecognized forms, warmed
  residual reuse and an asserted signal. The Jacobi decline cases establish
  optional recognition limits, not invalidity of the represented mathematics.
- The log-kernel oracle uses directed 2048-bit MPFR logarithms and exact GMP
  rational combinations, including sign-aware bounds for shift*ln(2). The
  approximation interval must contain the full independent reference enclosure.
  The 22 residuals in two forms yield 880 fresh/warm assertions; eleven residuals
  at nine shifts yield 1980. Shift endpoints are logarithmic coefficients, not
  enormous binary integer allocations. Fresh nodes do not clear global caches,
  and finite containment is not a correctly-rounded conversion assertion.

## Hyperreal exponential/root kernels and negative-tail corpus (2026-11-27)

Baseline: e6743c8718ad2d7c2e8bf74e65817b7e9f0505ff. Whole-file review of
computable/approximation/exp_sqrt.rs (276 baseline lines),
computable/approximation/exp_tail_tests.rs (39), tests/negative_exp_tail.rs (139)
and tests/support/representations.rs (141): 595 lines. Hyperreal owns the
one-unit approximation, mathematical domain, cancellation, source retention
and fixture/replay contracts (P1–P7, P19). Missing witnesses were Rustdoc for
all 22 named declarations, including the function-local guard constant and
three fixture fields, and accurate descriptions of the finite test evidence.
Twenty selected unit tests, six negative-tail integration tests and eleven
representation/replay consumer tests passed on the baseline before edits.

The documentation now separates the kernel paths and their preconditions:

- A sufficiently negative exponential can return a zero integer at a requested
  precision while retaining its strictly positive exact source. The BigInt
  tail threshold handles both i32 endpoints; this does not establish full
  endpoint support for the ordinary series, other kernels or interval APIs.
  The small exp/expm1 series use certified ranges and guard estimates rather
  than treating a term estimate as a total-work bound.
- The square-root kernel consumes a retained Square child through absolute
  value's 1-Lipschitz identity. Otherwise it uses magnitude facts/refinement,
  an integer seed when planned msd/2-p <= 59, and recursive Newton refinement
  above that threshold. Rust division truncates negative odd exponents toward
  zero; the estimate is not an exact root binade. The usual four-guard-bit
  seed and older even-precision fallback both use integer arithmetic.
- The nth-root kernel checks degrees 3..=9, retains a nonnegative-radicand
  precondition, and encloses the guarded root between floor_root(A-1) and
  ceil_root(A+1). Its local constant describes the four-bit midpoint guard.
  A checked precision-product failure delegates to exp/ln, whose own domain
  and resource limits remain. That fallback does not prove total behavior
  at extreme precisions or independently handle zero through logarithms.
- Cancellation behavior is path-specific: exp can return zero/partial sums,
  expm1 has no initial poll, sqrt can discover magnitude before its explicit
  one-placeholder poll, and nth_root does not poll around integer root/power
  arithmetic. Partial integers are not completion receipts. The sqrt magnitude
  helper uses the operand's attached signal, not the separately passed signal.

Corrected the Newton comment's denominator from last_appr/2 to 2*last_appr,
matching both the implementation and the Newton formula. Replaced the stale
fixed-size/crossover narrative with the actual request-sized seed dispatch,
removed the unsupported extreme-precision totality claim and an orphan cosine
comment. No algorithm or threshold changed, and no new performance claim is made.

Test descriptions distinguish 315 dyadic argument/precision pairs with 630
strict directed-MPFR endpoint assertions from the eight-request extreme-tail
shortcut test. Integration smallness permits zero; positivity is checked
separately. The two-order refinement test does not explicitly demand a coarse
zero integer. The 164 exact integer-log identities accept no approximation.
Cancellation is pre-stopped, followed by clearing/retry and then four workers;
it is not an in-flight cancellation race. JSON bytes are compared before/after
warming, while CBOR is replayed without a byte-equality assertion. No fresh
process or reset shared caches are claimed. RUST_MIN_STACK was unset and these
checks set no enlarged stack; completion is not a measured stack bound.

The shared fixture defines 22 positive construction recipes with expected public
StructuralKind values. Its diagnostic labels are not proof of private variant
identity or enum completeness. Pi-scaled trig examples are pi/5, not a fifth
of a full revolution. Tests and fuzz consumers retain their original recipes,
order and assertions. Other consumers of the unchanged fixture implementation
were not rerun in this batch.

After the final edits, all twenty selected unit tests passed in both feature
configurations. Negative-tail integration passed five tests without optional

replay consumer tests passed with all features, as did five downstream Hyperlimit
resolver tests. Existing seed tests use directed MPFR bounds; the selected

## Arithmetic approximation kernels and precision exponent regressions

On baseline 3cfb31164c7c5d74a7ccbcfe90568e059ff9b4c6, read every line of
computable/approximation/arithmetic_kernels.rs (264 lines) and
computable/approximation/precision_tests.rs (32 lines), both under
crates/hyperreal/src/. These 296 lines are new whole-file review credit.
The owning layer is Hyperreal's integer approximation machinery, with P1–P7
and P19 governing exact source retention, certified magnitude use, cache order,
resource honesty, failure, and subsequent consumption. The admitted arithmetic
inputs are valid child expressions, nonzero reciprocal denominators, rational
weights with representable magnitudes, and representable working precision
arithmetic. Those implementation restrictions do not narrow the target contract.

All thirteen functions lacked Rustdoc, including the function-local weighted
helper. Added fourteen blocks: eleven kernel/helper declarations, two tests,
and one test-module overview. Recorded units of 2^p, operand ordering, magnitude
anchors, rounding, signal propagation and unchecked precision arithmetic.
Corrected inline comments that equated dropping a small addend with an unchanged
answer, or claimed one small product operand alone sufficed for a zero result.
Removed the unattached exponential-range comment at the arithmetic file's end.
The missing acceptance witness was declaration-level documentation plus private
rendering; forty-four existing selected unit tests passed before editing.

Reciprocal magnitude division rounds its integer quotient to nearest with ties
away from zero. Rational scaling truncates toward zero; nonnegative rational
precision then uses the scale helper's ties-toward-positive-infinity rounding.
Neither route promises correctly rounded evaluation of the original exact real.
The reciprocal's 16,384 scale guard runs only after a zero divisor sample is
refined; it is not a universal precision, allocation or total-work bound.
Magnitude queries use child-attached signals, whereas samples receive the
explicit signal. The caller remains responsible for rejecting abort placeholders.

A contained debug probe reproduced native Computable::zero().inverse().approx(0)
returning integer zero, while Real::zero().inverse() returned DivideByZero.
This is an existing native invalid-domain gap, not a valid reciprocal or a change
in the P6 target. No behavior was changed in this documentation batch.

The fixed three-term sum preserves index order, gives each rational product
eight coefficient guard bits, and accumulates four bits below the target before
rounding. An unavailable Rational::msd_exact currently skips the term. Inspection
of the shared magnitude helper confirms None includes both zero and an exponent
outside i32; this is not a proof that every skipped weight is zero. The latter
case was identified from control flow, not reproduced by allocating a rational
with more than two billion bits. It remains an implementation gap. Zero-weight
shortcuts also do not validate hidden coefficient-domain errors.

A source-extracted bound_log2 probe compared 65,933 distinct signed inputs near
powers of two and on a fixed grid against exact integer bit lengths. On this
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu host with rustc 1.100.0, only the two signs of 2^29-1
used an extra bit; no sampled result underestimated the integer expectation.
The three invalid signed inputs i32::MIN and either sign of i32::MAX panicked
in the debug build. This finite host measurement is neither exhaustive input
coverage nor an all-platform proof for floating logarithms. Binary64 here plans
guard bits and does not replace the authoritative scalar. Probes were limited
to 1 GiB address space, ten CPU seconds, fifteen wall seconds and no core dumps.
The same observations were reproduced after the final edits.

The precision tests retain 252 comparisons across nine sample bit widths,
seven selected precisions, two integer endpoints and two signs. Their i64 oracle
checks representable exponents; two further cases require rejection by panic of
an exponent above i32::MAX. Neither test proves all kernels accept extreme
precision inputs, nor does the panic implement a typed resource outcome.

After the final source edit, all forty-four selected tests passed with no default
features and with all features. These include magnitude planning, near-cancelled
reciprocals, operand-order multiplication, repeated powers, additions and deep
chains, rational samples, a three-term coefficient consumer, offsets and inverse
trig/hyperbolic consumers. Five downstream Hyperlimit resolver tests passed.
Private cargo doc passed both configurations with warnings and broken/private
links denied. Ten kernel blocks matched actual private Rustdoc pages; the local
weighted helper and three test/module blocks passed source inventory and
supplemental Markdown rendering. Ordinary library Rustdoc does not emit these

The arithmetic file has only four raw executable-token differences: trailing
commas removed by Rustfmt. Its tokens match an independently formatted baseline;

## Inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic approximation kernels

On baseline 9fd5731832e52662af78274d590476739b71b25d, read every line of

crates/hyperreal/tests/serde_asinh_ranges.rs (144) and
serde_atanh_rational_ranges.rs (175). These 1,108 lines are new whole-file
review credit. The owner is Hyperreal's retained-function approximation and
replay layer, under P1–P7 and P19. The domain includes principal real inverse
functions, their admitted rational/computable children, applicable small-series
ranges, replayed nodes, nonzero integral reciprocal atan denominators and
representable working precision. Mathematical domains remain distinct from
implementation resource restrictions and local convergence preconditions.

All thirty-four function declarations lacked Rustdoc. Added thirty-six blocks,
including the coefficient helper/test, nine integration helpers/tests and two
integration module overviews. Documentation records exact identities, units of
2^p, range and sign preconditions, direct versus deferred construction, guard
precision, abort placeholders/partial sums, and unchecked precision/counter

Generic atan rechecks a sample-certified half interval; rational and two-step
half-angle fallbacks avoid selecting the same borderline prescaled schedule.
Asin and atanh generic series reserve a sample-error unit to prove the eighth
interval. Asinh uses a half-interval proof and sign-separated fallback. Its
coarse request must pass the range proof before zero can be returned; the
asin/atan global principal-angle bounds justify their different coarse paths.
None of these local range checks replaces full domain admission where required.
Rational small-series routes differ: nonzero asin/atanh metadata at most -4
proves strict magnitude below 1/8, while asinh metadata at most -2 proves
strict magnitude below 1/2. Missing metadata is not a smallness certificate.

Negative acos retains a nonnegative magnitude r and computes acos(-r), not
acos(r) for a signed negative payload. The square-root atan flag chooses between
sampling the retained rational square and squaring the integer root sample;
it does not prove rationality or exactness of the sampled square. Deferred
acosh/asin/acos identities retain their caller-admitted domains, while asinh's
identities hold for every finite real argument and use sign normalization to
avoid cancellation when the sign is known. Native wrappers add no separate
typed domain checks or total resource bounds.

The four ordinary rational atan anchor intervals were checked with independent
exact Fraction arithmetic and monotonicity of (x-a)/(1+a*x). Closed enclosing
residual ranges are [-1/18,0] for anchor 2, [-1/18,2/29] for 3/2,
[-1/8,2/23] for 2/3, and [-1/9,1/7] for 1. Branch boundaries and trace order
remain unchanged. Code inspection also identifies a restriction: a positive
noninteger input above two with an exponent outside i32 cannot take the
metadata-guarded reciprocal route, and its final half-anchor fallback has no
established small-residual bound. This extreme coefficient case was not
allocated or executed; the limitation is static control-flow evidence, not a
claim of observed completion or an alteration of the target support contract.

Removed the integral-atan comment's unsupported error-budget conclusion: its
listed fractions add to 11/8, so that text did not prove an error below one
unit. Replacement comments describe exact-denominator division, guard precision,
term stopping and final rounding without inventing a new universal proof.
This comment defect does not by itself demonstrate incorrect kernel results.
Also replaced an unmeasured speed assertion for the root-sample square path
with its actual calculation, corrected atanh's shared half-argument identity
wording, corrected the fixture identity sinh(1) = (e-1/e)/2, and removed
redundant small-series headers superseded by full Rustdoc.

The wide coefficient helper's positive-i32 products fit u64; exact integer
arithmetic verified the maximum endpoint. Its unchanged test compares sixteen

Existing working/coarse-cache regressions include 624 and 46,050 counted checks,

The asinh replay fixture covers six signed large graph spellings, native

Native intervals need only overlap broad bounds; finer Real intervals must
lie inside them. Subsequent addition and stable serialization remain separate

not for all internal fixed-point error bounds. The numerical cross-reference

## Shared-constant kernels, dispatch and e/pi qualification

On baseline 7a82b3407da77accfa95bf4231d2acae132aedd4, read every line of
crates/hyperreal/src/computable/approximation/constants.rs (233 lines),
approximation/dispatch.rs (161), approximation/e_plan_tests.rs (113), and
computable/approximation.rs (97). These 604 lines are new whole-file review
credit. The owning layer is Hyperreal's retained-expression evaluation, under
P1–P7 and P19: exact recipes, justified approximations, shared-cache reuse,
explicit cancellation/resource limits and downstream consumption. Mathematical
inputs include valid retained nodes and constant identities; binary-split
helpers additionally require nonempty intervals (and a positive starting index
for the factorial series). Precision representability is not a total-work bound.

All thirty-seven declarations lacked Rustdoc. Added thirty-nine blocks covering
constants, functions/methods, test modules and two file/module overviews. Missing
witnesses were complete source documentation and private rendering. Baseline
checks passed nineteen selected unit tests and five named-certificate replay
tests. Supporting reads located cache lookup/publication in the outer Computable
evaluator, not in these recipes or only in constructors. Dispatch keeps every
payload and selector, including the Carlson/Legendre choices and Jacobi component
indices; no arm, evaluation order, predicate or test was changed.

The shared table has eighteen dense slots. That count does not bound integer
bytes, and cache_index is not itself a wire-format serializer. SharedConstant's
approximation routine evaluates a recipe; its own cache lookup is outside it.
Tau directly calls the pi kernel at p-1 after outer lookup, and that call alone
does not populate pi's separate slot. Cross-constant reuse and abort-aware
publication belong to the outer layer. Raw internal nodes bypass recognition
when the same shared log/root constant is being filled; they do not validate
an arbitrary payload or supply an independent domain proof.

Chudnovsky handles fractional pi requests first, using 64 guard bits and
ceil(work_bits/43)+2 terms; coarse or declined requests use the exact Machin
identity. Binary splitting checks the stop flag on recursive entry and once
after splitting, but its integer products and the later root/division work
have no local interruption guarantee. The Option result combines conversion
or arithmetic decline with cancellation, not typed resource exhaustion.
Positive p and i32::MIN decline in pi_chudnovsky before splitting; pi's Machin
fallback still has unchecked working arithmetic. Balanced recursion is a depth
property, not a work or memory budget.

Independent exact Fraction arithmetic checked 640320^3/24, the stated
Chudnovsky consecutive-term bound (the k=0 ratio and the uniform k>=1 upper
bound 27648/640320^3 < 2^-43), the ln2 rational-product identity, and the
rational atan anchor identity. The documented e-split recurrence agreed with
direct rational summation on 198 finite intervals in a separate mathematical
check. This last comparison verifies the described recurrence, not execution
of the Rust helper; the native direct-e regressions exercise its implementation.
These checks are not a complete proof of every fixed-point kernel error bound.

The e planner keeps a downward-rounded factorial lower bound using u128
multiplication and a 64-bit mantissa. Returning n excludes the threshold-crossing
(n+1)th term; the exact truncated sum is rounded only after adding its initial
one. Its tail is still an approximation error, not an exactly represented e.
Nonnegative precision requests currently select three terms. A source-extracted
Rust probe reproduced that result at 0, 1 and i32::MAX, and a debug panic at
i32::MIN before large work. The observation was identical before and after edits;
the probe was contained to 1 GiB address space, ten CPU seconds, fifteen wall
seconds and no core dumps. That unsupported precision and the lack of an inner
e cancellation poll remain implementation limits, not target-contract changes.

The e tests retain 4,151 distinct factorial-threshold requests and a finite
at-most-one-extra-term sentinel, which is not a universal optimality claim.
Ninety-three direct evaluations through precision -262144 use strict directed
MPFR enclosures. Shared refinement checks seven nonmonotone requests through
retained and new handles plus exp(1); it does not assume a cold process cache.
The stop/retry test discards its first result and checks the later enclosure,
without asserting that inner computation stopped or inspecting the aborted
cache. Its serde section checks four same-process replay precisions.

The pi test retains thirty-two direct requests from one to 120,700 fractional
bits. It permits one integer unit of difference from a nearest-rounded MPFR
reference at 192 extra bits, then checks dispatcher agreement. This differs
from the strict directed e enclosures and is not a universal rounding proof.
The pi abort test starts with an already asserted flag; it does not exercise a
mid-computation stop, publication or retry. Module documentation keeps these
qualification claims distinct from those of neighboring included kernels.

Replaced unverified timing comparisons with the actual Chudnovsky/Machin
selection and balanced arithmetic. Corrected the claim that constructor code
owns cache selection, the suggestion that a warm atan anchor leaves only series
work on every later call, and wording that treated the truncated factorial sum
as the whole infinite tail or rounding as the sole source of cache stability.
No new performance, memory bound, universal precision or completeness claim is
made. The implementation and its branch choices remain intact.

The selected unit checks include direct e/pi, shared cache reuse across handles
and threads, pi/tau transport and inverse-function consumers. This is focused

pages; sixteen test-only blocks passed source inventory and supplemental

## Trigonometric approximation kernels and coarse-result gaps

On 2026-11-27, reviewed all 995 baseline lines of
crates/hyperreal/src/computable/approximation/trig.rs at
f0d53a8431d8b6cdda532f8ba3a4401b311def21. All thirty-one functions lacked
Rustdoc. Added thirty-one blocks describing their mathematical roles, exact
source relationships, sample units, range assumptions, cancellation behavior
and limits. The owning layer is Hyperreal's scalar approximation implementation
(P1–P7), with cache/refinement and replay implications for P4 and P19. The
missing acceptance witness was private rendered documentation of these kernels;
additional probes reproduced existing numerical gaps on the target revision.
This is a documentation change, not a repair or certification of those gaps.

The domain includes caller-reduced Computable arguments, exact rational leaves,
retained pi/rational differences and equally scaled integer component samples.
Sinc and cosc continue analytically through zero with values one and one half,
under the constructor's magnitude-at-most-three-quarters certificate. Imported
tags alone do not establish local Taylor ranges. Generic sine/cosine/tangent
kernels nominally consume magnitude below one, while native tangent scheduling
can pass magnitude below two. Those are distinct facts, not a proof that every
scheduled request meets every local error argument.

Reproduced incorrect coarse tangent/cotangent results with a public native probe:

| Expression | Cold approx(1) | approx(1) after approx(-64) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| tan(7/5) | 0 | 3 |
| tan(3/2) | 0 | 7 |
| tan(39/5) | 0 | 9 |
| Imported PrescaledCot(1/64) | 0 | 32 |

These are integer approximations in units of two. Independent exact Fraction
bounds show all four mathematical values exceed two, so each cold zero lies
outside even a one-unit error allowance. For the first two, positive cosine
and alternating sine/cosine bounds yield tangent lower bounds 14140/2701 and
120/11. For 39/5, a Machin-series pi enclosure bounds the positive complement
5*pi/2-39/5 below 2/35, giving a cotangent lower bound above two. The last
lower bound is 8191/128. Thus the failure claim does not rely solely on warm
and cold wrappers disagreeing. It concerns the magnitude-free p>=1 shortcuts
in the medium-rational complement, generic tangent, large-rational tangent and
generic cotangent kernels. The rational tangent helper's admitted magnitude
below one does justify its coarse zero; it is not the same domain.

The probe's output was identical before and after documentation edits, including
fine results and fixed-sector dispatch counts. Each run was contained to 1 GiB
address space, ten CPU seconds, fifteen wall seconds and no core dumps. The
initial trace probe omitted the recording scope and failed its count assertion;
adding that scope corrected the probe, without loosening the expected count of
one. No production test, fixture, trace order or implementation was changed.
The coarse errors remain implementation gaps relevant to P1/P4/P6, requiring
future executable regressions and a code fix outside this docs-only batch.
Existing passing fine-precision tests do not certify these coarse requests.

Corrected the fixed half-pi sector description: positive multiples are two on
[7/2,39/10], three on [79/20,27/5], four on [11/2,7], and five on (7,8).
Negative arguments reflect those choices. Earlier branches own endpoints;
the magnitude-exponent-two guard excludes [8,17/2] despite the last written
comparison. Exact Machin-series rational bounds verify residual magnitude below
one on all four enclosing intervals. The probe confirms that 701/100 chooses
five, -701/100 chooses minus five, seven chooses four, and eight misses the
fixed table. Four is independently nearer for 701/100; nearest-multiple wording
was incorrect, but choosing five still leaves an admitted small residual.
Neither observation alone establishes a reduction bug.

Documented the quotient estimator's one-step correction, large-exponent guard
request, and signal distinction between attached estimator/fallback graphs and
explicit residual evaluation. Direct residuals retain r-m*pi/2 or r-m*pi/4;
they are generally irrational, not exact rational residuals. Their integer
samples do not replace the exact source. The quarter-pi shortcut tests a guarded
sample against +/-128 at precision -8, rather than deciding exact equality at
a half-radian threshold. Its selected quotient identities and additional guard
bits differ from the adaptive division path.

The integer divider rounds the supplied rational quotient with ties away from
zero, requires nonpositive precision whose negation fits, and panics on a zero
denominator. It does not itself propagate component errors or prove a nonpole.
Adaptive division assumes bounded trig components: denominator magnitude controls
twice as many additional source bits; a zero sample requests eight more. A ready
quotient returns before the stop and 16384-extra-bit guard checks. That guard
is neither a total-work budget nor a proof of a pole. Component work, leading-bit
casts, precision arithmetic and series counter products retain unchecked limits;
entry-stop placeholders and interrupted partial sums require caller rejection.
No universal precision, cancellation or memory bound is claimed.

Replaced unverified timing assertions with concrete scheduling and arithmetic.
Corrected two pseudocode factorial denominators, and removed an orphan trailing
log1p comment. Preserved all executable choices. The baseline selected suite
passed eighteen unit tests and six replay/composition integration tests with all
features. After the final source edits, eighteen selected unit tests passed in
each of the no-default-features and all-features configurations; the same six
integration tests and five downstream Hyperlimit resolver tests passed. Selected
coverage includes ordinary and huge rational reductions, small-angle quotients,
owned rational paths, imported cotangent domains and certificate composition.
The many-digits regression checks numerical expectations, despite a name referring
to one high-precision pi pass; it does not assert that pass count. Numeric oracle
tolerances remain unchanged and do not constitute universal kernel error proofs.

Private cargo doc passed both configurations with warnings and broken/private
links denied. All thirty-one blocks matched their actual private library pages;
no supplemental test-only rendering was needed for this file. Independent token
comparison found only three optional commas removed by Rustfmt, and identical

Rustfmt and git diff --check passed. No focused validation remains blocked;

The inverse stores psi and log(b/a), reconstructing positive r=(b/a)^2 as an
exponential. Its working variable s=asinh(tan(phi)) makes the forward derivative
r/(1+(r-1)*tanh(s)^2), bounded by min(1,r) and max(1,r). The rational forward
helper uses odd symmetry and decaying exponentials; it selects oblate/prolate
corrections from the exact rational r endpoint, not by attempting to decide
whether an arbitrary computable r equals one. For negative s the r-endpoint
order reverses. Residual narrowing, signed interval division, certified signs
and outward dyadic rounding shrink the clipped root enclosure.

At p<=0, K=4-p and root width 2^(p-4) determine the temporary clipped search.
The monotone latitude map is 1-Lipschitz. Its tail satisfies
pi/2-g(K) < 2*exp(-K) < 2^(1-K) = 2^p/8, using exp(1)>2.
Root midpoint, elementary evaluation and rounding allowances contribute
1/32, 1/8 and 1/2 output units; together with clipping the sum is 25/32.
The node continues to represent the original equation, and K grows on finer
requests. These conditional mathematical bounds require admitted inputs and
completed child enclosures; they do not prove every machine precision or
resource path. Coarse p>=1 zero is valid from the latitude range, unlike the
unbounded tangent shortcuts recorded in the preceding batch.

All 667 lines were reviewed. The twenty-seven Rustdoc blocks include twenty-five
new blocks and two existing public operation descriptions. Impl blocks, private
constructors, kernels, test modules, tests and the local MPFR reference function
are accounted for. The owning layer is Hyperreal (P1–P7), with replay and

RF admits nonnegative x,y,z with at most one zero; RD admits nonnegative x,y
with at most one zero and positive z. Public admission resolves signs in x,y,z
order before collective rejection. A failed sign query propagates Exhausted
before the collective invalid-domain check; it is not an assumed zero. Diagonal
recognition follows successful validation. Only a proved zero is permuted to the
first argument; RD's third argument is never swapped. The native payload stores
[root_x,log_y,log_z], reconstructing [root_x^2,exp(log_y),exp(log_z)]. Its positive
sign fact relies on finite valid children, not on a raw enum tag validating
arbitrary imported graphs. The constructor inherits the first present child
signal rather than merging all signals. Corrected the old comment that called
every finite deserialized payload valid without qualifying its children.

Documented the directed quotient's exact floor/ceiling role, nonzero-denominator
precondition, zero shortcut and small-positive quotient shortcut. The latter
avoids an enormous denominator when the negative shift already exceeds the
numerator's bit length. Host shift/allocation limits and lack of a stop poll
remain explicit; debug assertions are not typed domain admission.

For the mean enclosure, ordered nonnegative intervals use an even grid q,
which can be positive or negative in the helper. Lower-endpoint sum S and
absolute deviations D_i=abs(3L_i-S) give D=max(D_i), N=sum(D_i^2), H=4S(S-D).
The strict checks D<S and N<H establish the spread and G=N/H assumptions.
The mean-scaled integral RF*sqrt(mean) is bounded by one and 1+G/(5(1-G)). Monotonicity selects upper input endpoints
for the lower bound and lower endpoints for the upper bound. Integer root and
quotient bounds preserve scale when q is even; the helper does not validate
that parity or input ordering. None declines this bound, not RF itself.

The duplication kernel starts at q=2*(min(p,0)-16), widens child samples and
uses known nonnegativity to clamp endpoints. RF is invariant under duplication;
RD accumulates positive terms while scaling its remainder by successive quarters.
RF tries the mean bound and then the min/max bound every fourth iteration;
RD checks its accumulated sum and remainder every iteration. Only an enclosure
width at most two on the p-3 grid permits return. Its midpoint radius contributes
at most one eighth of an output unit, and rounding at most one half: the sum is
five eighths. An unresolved denominator or exhausted iteration schedule restarts
with twice the grid accuracy, rather than permitting a partial success.
Checked grid-overflow panics and unbounded child/integer work remain distinct
from typed resource exhaustion. Stop polls do not interrupt each integer
operation, and interrupted zeros require rejection by the outer caller.

The three unit regressions retain 3,520 exact rational quotient cases, both
integrals' maximum coarse/preexisting-stop requests, 972 candidate repeated-
argument mean-enclosure cases, a near-diagonal spread and three declined domains.
An independent exact applicability calculation admits 837 of those candidates;
the retained Rust test asserts only more than 500, not that exact count.
Repeated-argument references use reciprocal square root, acos or acosh at
768-bit MPFR precision, followed by even-grid homogeneity. They do not use
Carlson duplication. Nearest-rounded comparisons are not strict directed MPFR
enclosures. The near-diagonal test containing one does not assert that the
slightly spread RF equals its diagonal reference.

The integration oracle normalizes with u=sqrt(z/(t+z)), using z=4 and
A=1-x/z, B=1-y/z in [0,3/4]. Corrected the old unnormalized substitution
comment to agree with the coefficient recurrence. Its 2048 coefficients give
RF/RD weights 1/(2n+1) and 1/(2n+3), followed by 1/sqrt(z) and 3/z^(3/2).
Exact rational checks confirmed eighty coefficients of the underlying binomial
convolution identity, the mean correction-factor identity across the finite
applicability grid, and 4*(3/4)^2048 < 2^-840. The latter is an analytic tail
bound for the fixture range, not a complete MPFR rounding-error bound. Input
midpoints and 1024-bit arithmetic remain rounded reference computations; their
final exact binary rationals are test expectations, not production integrals.
These finite checks do not prove universal implementation correctness.

Documented the actual scope of diagonal/circular identities, symmetry and
homogeneity, the independent cyclic RD identity, 22 transformed scalar recipes,
six AGM endpoint fixtures, and normalized 1e-320/1e320 scale cases. Refinement
assertions require interval overlap, not nestedness or an independent oracle.
Cancellation starts with an already asserted flag. Concurrent reader checks
establish positive nondegenerate intervals. JSON/CBOR replay is within one
process, with structural equality and deterministic JSON separate from numeric
agreement; hostile graphs and fresh-process cache isolation are not covered.
Removed an unmeasured relative-cost assertion while preserving the exact
four-step RF checking schedule. No performance improvement is claimed.

For S=sin(r), C=cos(r), Y=C^2+c*S^2, the first-kind principal formula is
S*RF(C^2,Y,1). The second-kind formula is
S*C/sqrt(Y)+c*S^3*(RD(C^2,Y,1)+RD(C^2,1,Y))/3. On the closed chart C>=0
and Y>0, so nonzero terms have S's sign. The cyclic RD derivation is applied in
the chart interior; continuity extends the resulting finite formula to C=0.
At either endpoint the first term vanishes, Y=c, and the remaining expressions
are the appropriately signed complete values. The Carlson arguments remain
admitted with exactly one zero. This does not require applying the singular
cyclic identity itself at C=0 or narrowing the public amplitude domain.

For odd signed n, the shifted integrand's radicand is
sin(r)^2+c*cos(r)^2 = c*(cos(r)^2+sin(r)^2/c). Accordingly negate the local
log complement and scale F by c^-1/2 or E by c^1/2. Even n uses c directly;
all cases add n complete integrals. The node retains the exact amplitude and
subtraction, not a specific integer as its definition. Stop checks precede and
follow phase sampling; interrupted samples cannot be consumed as chart witnesses.
Subsequent expression construction adds no local polling or cumulative work,
heap-byte or precision budget. Child resource and publication contracts remain.

c40f8d309c8b2bbffff80104fd4ec936da9a3d46. Reviewed all lines of these files:

The 633-line review accounts for thirty-three Rustdoc blocks: thirty-two named
declarations and one oracle module overview, including thirty new blocks and
two reviewed public operation descriptions. The overview was revised. The owner
is Hyperreal (P1–P7), with exact defining relations, replay and supported subsequent
operations relevant to P19/P20. Missing acceptance was documentation of private
construction, local scaling recognition, clipped root refinement and the actual
scope of qualification fixtures. Inputs remain finite real values and parameter
m<1, including negative m, with continuous unwrapped inverses of F or E. The
original equations and all executable behavior remain unchanged.

Public admission computes log(1-m) before exact zero/circular shortcuts. Native
construction first cancels a matching forward kind with a structurally equal
parameter child, then builds the complete integral Q and seeks an integer
structural multiple of it. The local scaled helper visits at most 32 levels
per chain, peeling Negate, binary Offset and Multiply with a recognized rational
factor. It tries the left factor first. A nonmatching product is retained as a
single base with scale one, not recursively normalized; a zero budget declines
before inspecting the node. None declines the shortcut rather than reporting
scalar resource exhaustion. Rational recognition, multiplication and power-of-two
allocation are not bounded by that visit count. The shift helper's unsupported
negation of i32::MIN is a source-level limitation, not a newly executed extreme-
allocation probe or a new typed resource claim.

Matching residual bases and an integer ratio of rational scales recover an exact
multiple of pi/2. The complete scale is nonzero for the valid positive Q; nearby
values or merely value-equal but structurally different bases do not establish
that identity. Otherwise the original pair is boxed with any known input sign
and no magnitude bound. Input signal selection precedes parameter selection,
and native exact results retain the selected attachment. These constructors assume
valid finite children rather than validating arbitrary imported graphs.
The public result adapter first recognizes pi multiples, then uses the shared
identity conversion to recover recognized rational/pure-quadratic carriers or
retain the exact opaque Computable. It is not general canonicalization.

A contained public-API probe reproduced a cancellation-attachment gap in that
adapter for both kinds at m=3/4. Attach a clear flag to a complete integral Q,
then invert Q to exact pi/2 and assert the flag. The source retains its flag and
returns no enclosure; the recovered pi carrier has no attached signal and still
returns an enclosure. Its exact value is correct, but the public reconstruction
does not transport the native constructor's selected cancellation attachment.
Documented this existing behavior at elliptic_result; no implementation fix or
new cancellation guarantee is included in this docs-only batch. It remains
relevant follow-up for P5/P19 rather than evidence of end-to-end cancellation
support. The probe uses a fresh process with 1 GiB address-space, ten CPU-second,
fifteen wall-second limits and no core dumps.

Numerical reduction samples value/Q at precision zero, with the completed API's
at-most-one-unit guarantee. As in the preceding forward audit, that guarantee
puts the local root in the closed half-pi chart; it does not establish strict
interior selection or nearest rounding. Odd signed phases reciprocate c=1-m
and rescale the target by sqrt(c) for F or its reciprocal for E. The exact phase
angle and retained inverse definition remain distinct from numerical root work.
Cancellation is checked before a sampled phase can supply the chart witness.

For p<4, the solver takes k from the lower rational pi/2 enclosure at grid p-8.
The clipped root stays in [-k,k], with clipping gap at most 2^(p-7), and its
bracket narrows to width 2^(p-4). The derivative helper constructs sqrt(Y) or
its reciprocal, Y=cos(at)^2+c*sin(at)^2, at rational angles. That formula is
positive for every angle; monotonicity in absolute angle requires the principal
chart. Nearest/farthest absolute bracket endpoints bound the derivative without
deciding whether an arbitrary c is above or below one.

Working residual precision starts at -16 and is retained across outer iterations,
refining in 32-bit steps until the derivative lower bound is positive and the
residual width is at most that bound times current bracket width divided by
sixteen. Signed interval division, outward dyadic rounding, clamping and certified
residual signs then narrow the bracket. If the actual local root is outside the
inner clipped interval, the derivative argument applies between the midpoint
and the clipped endpoint; it does not extend a local bound beyond its scope.

Clipping, bracket midpoint, final evaluation and rounding allow respectively
1/128, 1/32, 1/8 and 1/2 output units, totaling 85/128. At p>=4, the omitted
local angle is at most pi/2; a two-guard-bit phase sample plus rounding gives
at most 3/4+pi/32 units at p=4 and a smaller omission thereafter. Exact Machin

The kernel receives an already constructed amplitude phi and ln(c), c=1-m>0.
It does not itself invert F. For kinds 0/1/2 it evaluates sin(phi), cos(phi) or
the positive square root of cos(phi)^2+c*sin(phi)^2. Sampling the exact quotient
2*phi/pi at precision zero gives an integer with error at most one, so the exact
residual lies in the closed half-pi chart. The previous strict-error/interior
comment overstated the consumed API guarantee. Corrected the explanation without
changing phase selection. Rotation by n modulo four handles negative phases;
positive weighted squares avoid subtractive cancellation in dn and remain valid
at both chart endpoints.

An explicit signal is attached to both cloned payload children. Entry, post-phase
and pre-final polls return a zero placeholder on stop; the caller must reject it.
The selected component delegates its requested binary precision to the exact
constructed expression. Invalid kinds panic unless a stop returns first. No new
cumulative work, heap-byte or latency bound is supplied; finite graph descriptions
and a precision exponent are not such bounds. Arbitrary invalid imported child
graphs are not admitted merely by naming the Jacobi tag.

Public tuple constructors validate ln(1-m) before even a known-zero shortcut.
The ordinary path shares the inverse amplitude across sn/cn/dn; the combined
path also forms E at that amplitude. With m=0, epsilon retains the input itself;
with u=0 the combined result likewise keeps it as epsilon. The component helper
recognizes integer pi/2 amplitudes structurally, uses exact public sine/cosine,
and chooses dn=1 or sqrt(1-m). Otherwise it constructs tags in component order
and invokes the shared exact result conversion. This is not numerical angle
recognition, a second domain proof or a guarantee of uniform cancellation controls.

## Statistical approximation and retained normal-quantile evidence

On 2026-11-27, reviewed the following whole files at clean rustdoc baseline
00f02d0a053879f74d4edf7e8e1c324e3a0da9c8:

| File | Baseline lines | Documented declarations |

The 552-line whole-file review is supplemented by two named-item reviews:
Computable::normal_quantile in computable/node/algebra.rs and
Computable::exact_normal_quantile in computable/node/structural_analysis.rs.
Only those items receive scoped credit; neither large containing file is claimed
complete. Twenty-four Rustdoc blocks cover twenty-three declarations and the
integration crate overview: twenty-three new blocks and one extended public
constructor description.
Hyperreal owns this contract (P1–P7, with retained composition/replay relevant to
P19/P20). The missing acceptance was documentation of the auxiliary series,
CDF-certified inverse search, exact reconstruction and actual reference scope.

For defined finite x, the auxiliary series is S(x)=sqrt(pi)*exp(x^2)*erf(x)/2,
not erf itself. The enclosing constructor supplies the Gaussian and normalization.
Terms begin at x and advance by 2*x^2/(2*n+3). A coarse sample at -10 estimates
squared magnitude and guard demand; the working operand receives eight additional
bits. A zero next term or a decreasing rounded-term geometric-tail criterion
stops summation before adding that next term. The exact term ratios eventually
decrease, but the implementation uses rounded terms and planning guards, not a
separately returned accumulated-error interval. Finite sample checks do not
establish that rounding/truncation bound for every magnitude and precision.
A stop in the loop returns a partial sum for the caller to reject; initial
planning precedes that poll. Growth can be exponential in x squared, with no
cumulative work or heap-byte budget.

The erfc, survival, interval and logarithmic wrappers construct exact expressions
and delegate refinement. They do not subtract independently rounded point values.
Nor do they implement separate asymptotic tail formulas. The interval kernel is
an oriented CDF difference and accepts reversed endpoints as a negative result;
public Real admission owns the ordered-interval rule. Log density instead uses
-x^2/2-ln(2*pi)/2 analytically, avoiding an exponentially small intermediate.
Public Real's practical input windows are distinct from these native definitions.

The quantile probe uses samples of the probability and CDF at trial-2/trial+2
working units, then the center when necessary. A sampled difference greater than
two units separates the two one-unit enclosures. Equal means a strictly enclosing
neighborhood, not exact trial/root equality; Greater/Less certify order. The
center permits progress when a neighborhood endpoint equals the root. Magnitude
only plans guard bits. Refinement saturates in sixteen-bit steps, with no
iteration cap; MIN is not a typed exhaustion terminal and can be retried forever
or encounter child arithmetic limits. Valid interior probability is a precondition,
not something this helper proves for arbitrary imported graphs.

Bisection trusts an inclusive input bracket at a grid four times finer than the
output. A successful neighborhood probe permits rounding trial/4; a final width
of at most four permits rounding (lower+upper)/8. Half-width plus nearest rounding
is at most one output unit, conditional on valid child enclosures. Positive output
precisions rescale a precision-zero result. Finer requests recursively obtain a
coarser certified bracket and propose one Newton correction; only a fresh CDF
neighborhood witness permits accepting the proposal. Otherwise they bisect the
old bracket. Coarse requests guard seed materialization using exponent plus bit
count, then expand from -1/+1 until strict CDF orders bracket the root. Neither
seed quality nor Newton convergence is accepted as a certificate.

The exact recognizer first handles rational one half. Otherwise a retained
Offset/Add/Multiply/ErfSeries shape suggests an argument, a quadratic projection
and perfect square root suggest a rational inverse, and complete native CDF
reconstruction must structurally match. A nearby-looking graph is insufficient:
the altered-CDF fixture changes its constant and requires a different result.
None declines optional recognition rather than deciding domain validity or
irrationality. The native constructor assumes (0,1), retains the raw seed and
exponent without adopting them as the quantile, and starts its outer signal unset.
It supplies no typed probability admission or new total resource bound.

the to_prec MAX fallback plus two; the series at x=1,p=MIN overflows -p; an ordinary three-quarter
quantile at output precision MIN overflows prec-2. The first two use the retained
series payload directly, not a claim about every public Real::erf dispatch path.
The probe catches the panics and records them; its successful process exit is
not successful library evaluation. Before/after result text is byte-identical,
with source-line movement in separate stderr logs. These remain P5/P6 follow-up
rather than typed exhaustion or an intentional domain migration. No release-

were 1 GiB address space, ten CPU seconds and fifteen wall seconds, with core
dumps disabled. Executable behavior is unchanged.

The quantile fixture's MPFR CDF is a nearest-rounded 384-bit point reference,
not a directed interval. Endpoint comparison uses strict monotonicity as its
mathematical motivation but does not certify exact CDF inequalities through
unbounded rounding assumptions. Corrected the previous overstrong plain comment
and documented this limit. No assertion or precision was weakened. This test file
does not register the shared backend-cache cleanup helper; no memory-lifetime
qualification is claimed for it.

The fixture covers five half-probability seeds, thirty probability/seed pairs

arguments and three seeds, and half-quantile replay uses three seeds and twelve

  rational is shared, but half() still constructs a fresh wrapper. Log/sqrt
  catalog misses are optional recognition failures, not domain decisions.
- Structural recognition from scalar equality. Ordered children and exact
  payloads participate; allocation identity shortcuts matching nodes. A false
  result cannot establish unequal values. Different quantile seed hints fail
  recognition, and separately allocated LinearCombination3 nodes have no match
  arm. The initial 64 charged comparisons bound only the recursive phase;
  iterative restart, identity-pair storage and bigint comparison have no global
  work/memory/cancellation contract here.
- Exact shared-perturbation order from tolerance Equal. The perturbation's
  certified sign determines the difference independently of the base's sign;
  only a certified magnitude below the tolerance permits tolerance equality.
- Nominal local trigonometric ranges from unchecked constructor tags, and the
  exact rational r from an irrational pi/2-r residual. Prescaled inverse-series
  tags schedule evaluation whose kernels independently check the series range.
  Existing tangent coarse-zero limitations remain explicitly qualified.
- Mathematical endpoint domains from constructor sign obligations. The generic
  positive-acos helper leaves its sign unknown, permitting a zero result at one.
  The rational positive-acos and both acosh constructors initialize Plus, so
  their callers must handle the zero-result endpoint first. These stricter
  constructor preconditions do not narrow the underlying operation's domain.
- Wrapper control from retained child control. Ordinary deferred wrappers attach
  no outer signal. Small-angle certification calls approx_signal with None;
  a successful sample of magnitude at most two at precision -2 proves
  abs(x)<=3/4 using the one-unit error allowance. Sinc/cosc retain the original
  signal only after that proof. Failure of this sufficient test does not prove
  the input lies outside the interval. Their removable zero values avoid a
  nonzero-denominator decision.

Baseline: a41e2b559d799640538ebe0459141777e39eaa81, branch rustdoc. Reviewed

those surrounding files receive no new whole-file credit here.

The owner is hyperreal expression construction, with P1–P7 exact structure,
conservative facts, domain admission, resource honesty and stable reductions;
consumers include checked Real operations and predicate resolution (P8–P11).
The input domain is defined finite exact-real graphs with each partial function's
real-domain preconditions and the direct root kernel's nonnegative degree-3–9
schedule. The missing acceptance witness was undocumented private helpers and

The review documents:

- Sqrt's sign-dependent absolute-value cancellation, exact-square scales,
  rational extraction and shared scaled radicals. The squarefree-named helper
  assumes prior decomposition, does not test squarefreeness and retains even
  a perfect-square payload. Native sqrt requires domain admission; a stored
  sign is not a negative-radicand check. Direct nth roots take nonnegative
  children even for odd degree; Real applies negative odd-root symmetry.
  The degree cap is an implementation schedule, not a mathematical bound.
- Named atan anchors, retained rational versus generic graphs, and series
  scheduling from certified binades or completed samples. At precision -4,
  sample magnitude at most seven plus its error permits abs(x)<=1/2. The
  evaluator rechecks its working range. Two half-angle steps bound the new
  argument strictly below tan(pi/8)=sqrt(2)-1; the binary shift transports
  result precision rather than adopting a rounded angle as authoritative.
- Atan2's principal branch, explicit zero-origin convention and absence of
  IEEE signed-zero distinctions. A known positive x needs no y sign; negative
  or zero x needs a resolved y sign. Unresolved x with already-known nonzero y
  admits y/(sqrt(x^2+y^2)+x), whose denominator is positive. If neither the
  sign search nor that fallback applies, try_atan2_until returns None and
  atan2's default -4096-floor wrapper panics. A precision floor is not total
  work, and these native APIs do not return a domain/cancellation receipt.
- Closed asin/acos domains versus open atanh and nonnegative acosh branches,
  exact anchors and eager versus deferred log/sqrt graphs. Planning magnitudes
  choose identities; they do not prove a tiny-series domain. Recognized rational
  binades, not an unrestricted magnitude claim, select asinh's small/large paths.
- Explicit outer-signal selection for inverse latitude and deferred atan;
  generic sqrt, axis constants and other reductions do not uniformly transport
  the original wrapper's signal. Log axis ratio encodes positivity only when
  that child is defined and finite. No constructor supplies a total-work budget.
- The cached-certified-binade or precision -8 sample used by the coarse inverse
  series range helper. Sample magnitude at most 31 plus its one-unit allowance
  proves abs(x)<=1/8 only after completed evaluation. Estimated exponents and
  cached zero metadata fall through to sampling. The helper has no stop poll
  or abort receipt, and false is only failure of this sufficient recognition.

## Computable diagnostic formatting and unit-fixture audit

Baseline: a13d1719c9596333b282334719d218d7ce5d394f, branch rustdoc. Reviewed
all 621 baseline lines of crates/hyperreal/src/computable/format.rs, including
all literal digit fixtures, 25 tests, their string helper, local bit planner,
placement payloads and trait implementations. Previous formatting entries audited
Real adapters and integration tests, not this implementation. Read its magnitude
search/sample/sign consumers, Real fixed/scientific delegation and checked
formatting alternatives. Those surrounding files receive no new whole-file credit.
The previously audited constants anchor was inspected but left unchanged.

The owner is hyperreal's diagnostic presentation boundary: P1/P4–P6 and P29
require that finite displayed digits not become exact scalar or zero evidence,
and that precision demand not be advertised as total resource control. Inputs
are defined finite computable sources, valid native precision plans and numeric
digit buffers satisfying the helper assumptions. The missing witness was absent
Rustdoc throughout the implementation and its unit fixtures. The edit adds 48
reviewed documentation blocks, distinguishing declared-item coverage from the
local helper and impl overviews. This is not a new formatting algorithm,
certified rounding contract or performance qualification.

The descriptions explain the actual representation and behavior:

- Buffers store most-significant-first numeric digit bytes, not ASCII. Trimming
  removes all trailing zeros and can empty an all-zero buffer. The increment
  helper preserves the length of an all-nine mantissa as 100... and returns an
  exponent carry. Empty input becomes [1] with a carry; its signed nine counter
  has no explicit large-buffer bound.
- The bit planner computes floor((places+4)*32/9), defaulting to 32 places and
  adding only a positive leading-bit estimate. It is a guard schedule, not a
  rounding proof. Unchecked usize/i32 arithmetic, narrowing casts, allocation
  and digit conversion do not produce typed numerical/resource receipts.
- Placement distinguishes scientific fractional mantissa digits from fixed
  fractional places; the latter includes the leading decimal exponent when
  selecting the number of extracted digits. Zero and zero-count branches are
  separate from ordinary extraction and trimming.
- Digit extraction normalizes an integer divisor, discarding remainders while
  shrinking it by ten. It increments only on a strict remainder comparison,
  with first-quotient-ten and all-nine exponent corrections. These operations
  do not establish a uniform decimal tie rule for the original exact real.
- Fixed Display limits leading-bit discovery by the requested absolute precision
  and clamps its magnitude estimate to zero. Scientific display uses the much
  deeper default search, including its unresolved-magnitude sentinel. Neither
  provides a total-work/output-allocation bound or numerical abort receipt.
  Known negative sources can display negative zero. Precision and explicit plus
  are consumed; width, alignment, fill, zero padding and alternate flags are not.
- Default formatting trims trailing zeros; explicit precision pads the requested
  fractional count. Checked Real conversion is identified separately, including
  its different notation-selection contract. Displayed text remains terminal
  approximate presentation, never authoritative scalar or interchange data.

Baseline: 73ff311c7fabe7c783c255764eed2200f9d9cae2 on rustdoc. Whole-file

The owning layer is hyperreal's retained expression graph, native import, and

reuse under P8–P11. Inputs include native recipes, exact rational and opaque
operand domains, signed integer approximation samples and i32 precisions,
packed cache facts, concurrent access, stop handles, and serialized graphs.
