- Computable clones share the recipe and node caches but carry their own stop
  handle; native serialization omits signals and accelerator facts and expands
  shared Arc contents into replayed values. Native decoding rejects recognized
  invalid domains and kernel ranges, but can leave opaque conditions unproved.
  Checked Real import additionally proves graph operand domains before comparing
  the imported class/payload, including when the outer scale is zero.
- Import validation checks children before parents, then tries interval filters
  and ordered conditions. False conditions yield ParseError; unproved conditions
  yield UnknownCertificate at the checked layer. The spilling traversal stack
  and local recognition counters are not total resource bounds. Domain-filter
  None means unresolved overlap, not necessarily equality. Affine-pi and Laurent
  recognizers retain their precise predicates, traversal order and bounded
  recognition roles; declining a recognizer does not refute the condition.
- Numeric cache installation uses a lazily allocated lock with atomic ownership
  transfer and exclusive destruction. Poisoned lock recovery retains its data.
  Equal or coarser samples do not replace a retained sample; strictly finer ones
  do. Downscaling rounds the stored integer to nearest with ties toward positive
  infinity, not the exact real itself. Unsigned precision-gap arithmetic handles
  the full i32 range. Raw storage has no stop check; the outer publication layer
  supplies that check and routes named constants through their shared cache.
- Tower storage retains the first successful value. The radical-decline bit
  permanently records a live-node attempt without retaining its cause or budget;
  it is not evidence of universal undecidability. No new retry guarantee is
  inferred. These are existing behaviors, not fixes to P4/P5 gaps.
- AtomicFacts bit lanes separate bounds, exact sign, scheduling demand and a
  selective inverse-trig-presence hint. Encoding accepts combinations that need
  not be mathematically consistent: callers supply the proof. Conditional stores
  protect resolved bounds; the unconditional bound store can weaken one. Sign
  publication preserves an already valid sign, with contradictory valid signs
  asserted in debug builds. Presence true cannot be cleared by a later false
  store. The hint's recognizer is selective; Tau and some unpropagated forms are
  outside it, so it is not an exhaustive graph-dependency predicate.

## Hyperreal structural certificates, interval filters and separation witnesses (27 November 2026)

Baseline: 6dd7c602c768de238ea41da7d9cadcd26c9c82a1 on rustdoc. Read every line
of computable/node/structural_analysis.rs (1549 baseline lines),
imported_domain_tests.rs (296) and fractional_separation_tests.rs (160), all
under crates/hyperreal/src. Total: 2005 baseline lines. Earlier scoped
exact_normal_quantile documentation remains part of the now complete file
review. Context reads included BoundInfo projections, the sign_until consumer,
Laurent normalization/inverse-trig relation code, exact float conversion, and
the existing algebraic/filter tests in node/tests.rs. These context reads do
not establish whole-file review of their containing files.

Owning layer: hyperreal structural evidence and optional scalar predicate
accelerators, under P1–P6 and downstream P8–P11. Inputs are valid retained
native recipes, finite exact rational coefficients, admitted real roots,
integer precision exponents, cached one-unit approximations, and optional
separation metadata. Native recipe domain assumptions are explicit: a cheap
sign recognizer is not an import validator. The missing witness was accurate
private documentation for each helper, field and traversal state, with actual
rendering and unchanged-behavior evidence. Eighteen selected all-feature unit
tests reproduced the baseline before editing: import recognition (eight),
fractional separation (four), algebraic separation/dependency/caps (three),
fractional reconstruction (one), and binary64 filters (two).

The structural file now has 118 reviewed blocks: three structs, seven named
fields, three impl overviews, five associated constants, fifty-six methods,
six local functions, three local constants, and two local Frame enums with
sixteen variants and seventeen tuple fields. The two test modules add nineteen
blocks, including their module overviews and the local wide fixture helper.
All 137 blocks explain roles and consumed invariants rather than restating names.

Key clarifications:

- The separation proof uses the nonzero integer norm of the integral numerator
  beta in alpha=beta/gamma. The previous wording could attribute an integer
  norm to the fraction itself. Numerator conjugate and denominator bounds give
  abs(alpha)>=2^-(denominator_log2+(D-1)*conjugate_log2) for nonzero alpha.
  The product of retained root degrees may overestimate the actual degree.
  Inversion swaps fraction bounds after a separate nonzero proof. For a root,
  gamma*root_n(alpha) is integral even with negative selected gamma; no false
  principal-root assumption on that integral numerator is needed.
- Rational-root dependency recognition tests positive same-degree roots using
  exponent combinations and exact perfect powers. Decline is not independence.
  A failed generator insertion leaves its append in the candidate; callers
  must discard that candidate. The parser memoizes completed nodes by live
  allocation identity and charges 256 previously unmemoized visits. Generator,
  degree, log, dependency and final-separation caps have distinct meanings;
  nested proof calls, coefficient work and allocations are not globally metered.
- The zero planner only returns -(B+2) within the requested floor. The consumer
  must still have a one-unit approximation with magnitude at most one to use
  the norm gap. A small numerical sample alone is not a zero certificate.
- Finite binary64 intervals are outward filters around an authoritative exact
  graph. Rational conversion requires integer components at most 2^53, basic
  operations expand rounded endpoints, and zero-crossing inverse/nonfinite
  results decline. The graph filter charges revisited shared nodes, recognizes
  selected Pi/E and arithmetic forms, and permits only normal-power offset
  multipliers. Its separate threshold helper constructs every representable
  power exactly and uses zero/infinity outside that range. Neither is a general
  floating-point replacement for scalar data or a native domain validator.
- Small-trig proofs peel binary offsets symbolically with an i64 sum and a
  32-visit allowance, polling only the peeled path. Reduced-pi recognition uses
  its own 32-inspection allowance and does not poll stops. The general materialized
  power-of-two rational helper instead allocates coefficients and negates negative
  exponents in i32: i32::MIN causes debug overflow. It has no allocation budget.
- Shared-constant cache lookup transports Pi/Tau samples with checked exponent
  shifts and may populate the other process-wide cache. Publication tests the
  supplied stop handle and strengthens only unresolved bounds from separated
  samples. Definite structural store_bound uses the unconditional setter and
  can replace stronger magnitude metadata; these are different publication rules.
- Cheap bounds try depth 24 before an explicit heap-stack traversal; that depth
  is not a total visit bound. Exact-sign discovery preserves cache/sample/Add
  relation order, then left-before-right arithmetic traversal and the final
  quadratic projection. Some direct cases recurse into children. Cached Unknown
  is an unresolved route, not undecidability, and separated samples can strengthen
  it. Domain shortcuts, zero annihilation and cached signs assume valid recipes.
  Cancellation is not blanket-enforced on these structural queries.
- Planning exponents may be inexact; certified projections withhold those hints.

functions. No new types or generated APIs are introduced. The public paragraph
is recorded separately from those blocks. Key reviewed behavior:

- Parameter compression scans selected Jacobi log-complement recipes and keeps
  an admitted quotient as an opaque scalar atom. It checks Inverse nodes in the
  traversed arithmetic skeleton, requiring immediate nonzero evidence before
  descending into their children. Other native function shapes are treated as
  already admitted leaves; it does not inspect every descendant domain. The old
  blanket comment about every hidden inverse was narrowed to the actual guard
  behavior, and the public normal-form paragraph now makes that precondition
  explicit. This documents implementation scope, not a relaxed admission policy.
- Arithmetic guard recursion visits left before right and short-circuits. The
  authoritative DAG scan pushes in stored order and therefore pops right before
  left, charging a visit before identity/depth checks. Live Arc identity is used
  only for that attempt's visited set. Temporary derived expressions must not
  enter it. Retained rational reductions stop a branch. The log scanner's depth
  zero is a successful no-op, whereas a guard/collection depth limit declines.
  Atom-cap or false-guard candidates are omitted without claiming full discovery.
- Native sign replay charges before reading an immediate sign, but that sign
  precedes depth, node and leaf-size checks. Cold replay handles selected
  arithmetic/rational trig forms; constant/exp shortcuts and cached facts assume
  defined operands. Query-root cancellation is polled at charged steps, not
  independently on every child signal. None conflates unsupported, unresolved,
  limit and stop outcomes. A retained relation root_sign can supply a result
  after nested replay declines, including a nested work-limit decline.
- Polynomial sign first partitions signed terms, then handles mixed signs only
  with fixed rational enclosures of positive shared constants. No atom is
  numerically refined. Quotient sign presupposes an admitted denominator: a zero
  numerator returns zero immediately. Completed principal-root relations expand
  and prove a nonnegative radicand in the same attempt, retaining the branch sign.
  These helpers are not independent validators for arbitrary malformed recipes.
- Native projection assigns sn atoms zero and other atoms one solely to propose
  a rational candidate. It must prove N-cD zero before accepting that proposal.
  Full quotient reduction follows; only failure of that reduction, rather than
  failure of its final rational projection, triggers the smaller numerator-only
  fallback. All original denominator obligations must already be admitted.
- Signed zero proof partitions a residual as P-Q with P,Q nonnegative at their
  selected values. Its sufficient square proof includes P=Q=0. Formal division
  can reduce the equality obligation even when the removed common factor can
  vanish. Common-monomial removal retains only the implication from a zero
  quotient back to the original zero residual, never a nonzero value or inverse
  certificate. Failed in-place work can leave a candidate partially changed;
  callers discard it. Re-sorting follows monomial removal because lexicographic
  word order can change.
- Root-completion handoff clears strategy-specific IDs/tables after one charge,
  preserving the same remaining counters and stop handle. It does not replenish
  budgets. A handoff with zero remaining nodes can succeed, but subsequent
  recognition declines. Query-local proofs alone do not publish global facts.
  The completed public adapter checks its root signal, publishes an exact sign,
  attempts first-success rational-tower retention and records the existing trace.
  It leaves the authoritative expression unchanged. Failure is not cached as
  irrationality or permanent undecidability. Counters/caps do not meter all
  structural-matcher work, peak allocation or elapsed time.

Twenty-nine blocks were reviewed: NativeRingRelation and its three fields,
NativeReduction and its four modes, three impl overviews, thirteen production
methods, one test-module overview and three test/helper functions. The docs
now explain:

- A relation a^p=N/H lives within its owning attempt's atom table. H is already
  proved nonzero at the selected values; dependencies use lower IDs. The record
  alone is not a replayable certificate or a complete selected-root definition.
  Its optional root_sign is supplied by root completion, not inferred from a
  square equation alone. Clone preserves query-relative data without reproof.
- Native atom admission first reuses structural matches, then tries square,
  completed-root and inverse-exponential relations in that order. Dependencies
  precede the new atom. Failed optional relations may leave an atom opaque;
  final cap/charge failure may leave disposable dependency state already changed.
  Scalar-product compression is a bounded representation choice, not a domain
  validator. Root completion changes which root products may remain opaque.
- Root-pair multiplication moves admitted rational squares into coefficients
  before checking retained degree, keeping parity and unrelated factors. Even
  a coefficient becoming zero does not bypass subsequent degree/work checks.
  The query-local Jacobi basis is chosen once per structural log-complement,
  reusing that choice across differently warmed copies. With h=1-m, the exact
  square identities use the selected sn or cn basis, and dn replays h from its
  retained logarithm. Native function domains remain caller preconditions.
- Reciprocal exponential relations recognize direct exp/E shapes whose summed
  logs cancel or leave an integral multiple of ln(2), producing a dyadic numerator
  over an earlier positive exponential atom. The existing log matcher has its
  own limits; the outer charge does not meter all its work. Derived expression
  expansion owns temporary atoms and never inserts temporary pointers into the
  authoritative DAG memo. Arithmetic order and original inverse guards remain.
- Substitution of a^p=N/H clears H^M. A monomial containing a^e becomes its
  other factors times a^(e mod p)*N^(e/p)*H^(M-e/p). Positive p, correct nonempty
  power tables and sufficient M are explicit private preconditions; malformed
  tables can panic. Exact accumulation enforces existing term/degree/coefficient
  limits. The power builder returns one for count zero without a charge and
  adds no separate allocation cap to its caller-supplied count.
- The reducer scans available relations by descending IDs and priority: roots,
  Jacobi dn, cn, then other relations. Quotient and Roots modes retain value;
  the latter uses only square-root relations. ZeroResidual and SignedZeroResidual
  retain only sufficient zero evidence, never a rescaled nonzero value. The
  signed mode additionally compares squares of nonnegative sides. Canonical
  zero may finish as soon as the substituted numerator disappears because
  denominator admission already happened. Optional factor-cancellation failures
  do not replenish the attempt's remaining work.
- Quadratic reciprocals use (a-b*r)/(a^2-b^2*q) for admitted r^2=q with rational
  q and nonzero rational norm. This does not require q to define an irreducible
  degree-two extension. A nonzero value such as 1+sqrt(1) can still decline this
  sufficient route because its conjugate norm vanishes. The earlier field-only
  plain comment was corrected to include rational-square/zero-root cases that
  the implementation already accepts.
- Graded formal division sorts a local remainder by total degree then sorted-ID
  lexicographic order, cancelling its leading term at each step. It returns a
  quotient only for zero remainder. Formal divisibility is not a nonzero witness
  for the divisor evaluated at selected atom values. Zero divisor, indivisible
  leading term and recognition limits decline. Counter charges cover explicit
  visits/arithmetic, not all sorting comparisons, coefficient internals or peak
  allocation. No numerical approximation or global scalar publication occurs.

The method audit documents several distinctions important to consuming these
helpers correctly. A charge polls the root signal before decrementing and
counts an explicit step, not all nested rational arithmetic, structural DAG
matching, allocation or sorting. Coefficient admission handles zero first,
otherwise rejecting oversized stored representation before canonical component
bit checks. Node, depth, atom, term, degree, coefficient and work caps remain
separate, with no claim of a complete heap/time resource bound.

Insertion checks degree and coefficient size before ignoring a zero coefficient,
merges exact matching terms and removes cancellations. A failed insertion leaves
that result unchanged while spending work. Empty-right addition and ordinary
zero multiplication can perform no charge; native multiplication has a distinct
entry charge and identity shortcut. Its cloned identity operand is already
admitted, rather than revalidated. Native root completion may collapse root
pairs before the retained-degree check; other paths check concatenated degree
before their optional relations. In-place root-pair reduction can leave partial
candidate changes on decline; an incoming product coefficient may already
exceed the stored cap before its next check.

Plain atom insertion compares structural recipes and has no extra initial
insertion charge or depth/stop poll; expansion supplies those entry checks.
This is not complete scalar equality. Plain expansion visits arithmetic children
left before right, checks every linear-form coefficient, and rejects extreme
binary shifts before materialization. It does not memoize shared arithmetic
expansions. Opaque shapes, including inverses, assume defined real values and
are not traversed as an import-domain validation pass. A completed plain-ring
projection checks cancellation, publishes only the exact sign and existing
trace, and returns the rational. It does not retain that rational in a tower;
a later call rebuilds its optional projection. Declines publish no negative fact.

dumps; these are external probe limits, not production completion guarantees.

were found in a disposable source copy with only the selected cfg(test)/test

Semantic findings recorded in the Rustdoc:

- RingQuotient carries a fraction and query-relative atom IDs, not a separate
  nonzero receipt. Its constructors trust denominator admission. Normalizing a
  zero numerator can discard that denominator only after its domain was proved.
  A formally nonzero polynomial is not proof of a nonzero selected value.
- Addition reuses equal denominators, and native addition can try divisibility
  before cross multiplication. Native multiplication can proactively cancel
  opposite factors. The former file-level claim that all factor search waited
  for expansion failure was too broad; only ordinary recovery is deferred.
  Zero absorption and cancelled cross numerators avoid irrelevant denominator
  growth, without excusing prior child/inverse admission.
- Projection establishes zero, a constant, or proportional stored terms,
  optionally after unit-circle reduction. Failure is not irrationality.
  Formal equality compares coefficient lists, not all values of dependent atoms.
- Quotient memoization uses live authoritative node pointers within one attempt.
  A hit checks positive depth, charges and polls, but consumes no node visit.
  A miss may recover only with the wrapper's original node/depth admission;
  completed children can remain after a failed parent. Strategy and atom tables
  must stay compatible. Entry counts are not retained-byte bounds.
- Expansion preserves left/right and three-term evaluation order. Inverse
  admission uses a retained nonzero sign or a local nonzero quotient proof.
  Native retained rational/parameter routes precede general arithmetic.
  Opaque native leaves retain a defined-real precondition; this recognizer is
  not a complete imported-domain validator. Inversion itself trusts its caller,
  including the nonzero proof for quadratic and retained square-root formulas.
- Ordinary exact division scans degree/lexicographic leading terms. With
  relation flags disabled it is formal long division; ordinary multiplication
  can apply enabled root/additional relations during subtraction. Native mode
  delegates to formal graded division. Neither route establishes that a divisor
  is nonzero at selected atom values. Limits can decline a mathematically exact
  quotient, and None is not a nondivisibility certificate.
- Optional cached factor reduction can consume the remaining work allowance
  and still return the original admitted quotient with changed=false. It does
  not overwrite the child cache. Recovery does not refund work or bypass an
  inverse guard; its arithmetic retry requires at least one child reduction.
- Conditional domain contradiction is rejection-only and invokes its supplied
  predicate at most once after projection and the final stop check. False does
  not validate a domain. It publishes neither conditional value nor sign.
  Defined-rational mode instead disallows opaque leaves before cancellation.
- Completed quotient queries publish an exact root sign and dispatch event,
  not a numerical sample or retained rational tower. Root-square mode must
  actually use the named sqrt(2)/sqrt(3) identity. Fresh attempts can retry;
  None combines limits, cancellation and unsuccessful proof search. Distinct
  node, work, degree and coefficient limits are not total-time/heap contracts.

products against integer fraction formulas and all 378 nonzero inverse cases.
They also checked empty/mismatched formal comparisons versus charged nonempty
comparison, zero-addition bypass, zero-numerator normalization after admission,
optional division's exhausted unchanged-result path, memo depth/stop/node
behavior, root-square usage gating, and sign-only final publication. No imported
undefined value was treated as an admitted geometry success. Probe processes

  root fact or perform its final completion poll; the outer query does that.

The reviewed contracts now distinguish:

  an enabled square table and compatible ordinary atom admission. It projects

  already have changed the coefficient; compacted prefixes and usage flags are
  also local partial state, not transactional outputs.

  need not be adjacent. Removing a pair changes no coefficient. The pi-only
  route relies on the caller's later coefficient guard; an empty monomial
  has no work charge or cancellation poll.
- Ordinary relation queries enable shared-root squares, rational root admission,
  trig argument congruence, exact rational trig projection and unit-circle
  reductions, but require additional_relation_used before publishing. A shared
  sqrt(2)/sqrt(3) square alone does not satisfy that gate. Extended queries use
  degree twelve and 32,768 charges without requiring a relation-use flag.
- Late factored-zero recovery runs only after quotient expansion declines at an
  Add root, using the same remaining work and child proofs. Projection failure
  after successful expansion does not invoke that fallback. Neither query runs
  earlier proof strategies on its own.
- Final cancellation checks precede exact root-sign publication and the distinct
  dispatch events. No numerical sample or retained rational tower is created;
  failure supplies no negative fact and a fresh attempt can retry. Counters and
  size limits are distinct from total arithmetic, elapsed time and memory bounds.

Ownership is Hyperreal's exact trig argument/value recognition over the guarded
quotient ring, P2–P6, with normal-form and predicate consumers under P8–P11.
Inputs require matching function/argument recipes, normalized query-local atom
IDs, compatible argument/relation tables, valid inverse witnesses and defined
opaque dependencies. The missing acceptance witness was item-level private

The Rustdoc records these distinctions:

- trig_atom first reuses structurally equal successful rational projections,
  then admits the argument and optionally attempts a new rational trig value.
  Failed optional projection can spend work before opaque admission proceeds.
  The positive cache is capped independently of successful uncached projections.
- Same-function argument quotient differences must project to exact zero before
  an atom is reused. Sine and cosine are not merged, nor are nearby arguments.
  Existing trig atoms require compatible argument-table entries; a missing
  entry declines rather than silently skipping it. Failed admission can leave
  local tables/flags changed. Native opaque domains and prescaled numerical
  kernel ranges are not universally validated by this helper.
- The dedicated congruence query requires trig_congruence_used, even after a
  rational result is found. It enables shared-root squares but not additional
  rational-root/trig-value/unit-circle relations. Final cancellation checking
  precedes exact root-sign publication and its dispatch event; no numerical
  sample or rational tower is retained.
- Rational trig projection recognizes ±atan(q)+k*pi/2 with rational q and a
  perfect rational sqrt(1+q²). It requires an atan atom, zero rational offset,
  coefficient ±1 and integral quarter turns. Explicit denominators must divide
  exactly first. Sufficient exact formulas and quadrant signs do not imply a
  complete rational-trigonometry recognizer; other kinds of recipe are outside
  the helper's sine/cosine precondition.
- A registered pair denotes retained/replaced square roles, not necessarily
  literal sine/cosine functions. Opposite kinds require equal arguments;
  same kinds require an exact pi/2 sum. Rational pi multiples have a cheaper
  comparison, while general complements use quotient arithmetic. At most the
  first matching pair is registered, without marking relation use yet.
- pi_multiple accepts only the stored one-term Pi shape and does not recognize
  zero as 0*pi. It is uncharged. quotient_is_half_pi maps failed exact division,
  including work exhaustion, to Some(false), meaning not proved. A failed final
  charge instead yields None; neither outcome is a certified inequality.
- Unit-circle reduction replaces c*rest*v² with c*rest-c*rest*u² using the
  recorded u²+v²=1. It preserves the implementation's term/pair/position search
  order and marks usage only after both insertions complete. The directed pair
  table is a precondition, not arbitrary cyclic rewrite input. No-match paths
  can return without a cancellation poll, and success means those rewrites
  completed, not that the result is zero or globally canonical. Outer queries
  retain completion and publication responsibility.

Test documentation now explicitly distinguishes raw symbolic fixtures from
numerical evaluation at unreduced prescaled angles. It also distinguishes
unsupported true identities from invalid ones: cos(-a)=cos(a) and
sin(pi/2+a)=cos(a) do not acquire proofs through the narrower implemented
argument rules merely because their mathematical identities are valid. Existing
None assertions were preserved; they are not descriptions of nonzero values.

The documentation now makes these distinctions explicit:

- Raw builders deliberately bypass simplification and may contain unproved

  are separate required inputs to the square relations.

  admitted cases and unknown/invalid domains. The preserved sin(1/3) case admits
  h=1+sin(1/3) and dn²=1+sin(1/3)*sn². Dyadic exponential pairs require exact
  log cancellation, not generic numerical closeness.
- The resource/retry test checks retained rational reuse under zero work,
  cancellation and four scoped readers. It is a finite concurrency witness,
  not a race-freedom proof. Cold-first and warm-first basis tests require one
  consistent choice per attempt, not identical choices between those attempts.
- Parameter compression checks inverse obligations through arithmetic wrappers
  before accepting a reusable atom. Formal storage probes intentionally use
  synthetic IDs to isolate term/degree/coefficient guards; these are not
  completed geometry admissions. Raw integer-angle sine atoms are not numerically
  evaluated to certify these limits.

  retained norm reuse, local inverse admission, zero/oversized/depth failures,
  and shared-root square relations without claiming every declined input invalid.
- The rectangular helper constructs sn=a+i*b, cn=f-i*g and dn=h-i*j, then the
  real parts of sn²+cn², dn²+m*sn², and dn²-m*cn²-(1-m), expected as 1,1,0.
  A proved negative parameter uses the reciprocal-complement transform with
  sqrt(1-m). Required roots, Jacobi calls and denominators are fixture-domain
  preconditions; unwrap failures are not returned typed outcomes. An unknown
  sign follows the nonnegative branch. The helper alone asserts no identity.
- The ellipsoid-axis test consumes scalar norm evidence through addition, hypot

  ellipsoid. Endpoint tests separately consume an exact zero in sine/cosine.
- Quadratic reciprocal tests require a nonzero conjugate norm as a sufficient
  recognizer condition. The nonzero value 1+sqrt(1)=2 deliberately declines that
  route because its norm is zero; that refusal is not a nonexistence proof.

addition denominator equals D under y=t/h. These are conditional algebraic

universal domain/closure proof. The same independent check confirmed the five

Baseline: `9bdd41420a91eca23ff032a0711dd03dd2715fd8` on `rustdoc`.

(857 baseline lines, 1086 after documentation) and `cyclotomic_zero_tests.rs`
(207 to 235): 1064 baseline lines in total. The 104 reviewed Rustdoc blocks
cover five structs, two enums, 12 named fields, 11 variants, 13 tuple payload

functions. Ordinary private Rustdoc rendered 87 blocks, a temporary test-enabled
Rustdoc build rendered 16, and supplemental Markdown rendering covered the local
Miller–Rabin base constant omitted by Rustdoc. Individual tuple-field anchors and
the three derived Clone implementations were inspected. This is selected-file
coverage, not repository-wide completion.

Ownership is Hyperreal's bounded exact scalar proof layer, P2–P6, with retained
sign evidence and downstream predicate/certainty consumers under P8–P11 and
P19–P20. The missing documentation witness was a complete account of field
admission, quotient-domain obligations, modular proof, resource accounting and
fixture scope. Baseline all-feature cyclotomic tests passed (nine tests).
Contextual reads of callers, pi-turn recognition, square extraction, facts and
Cargo profiles do not add whole-file review credit to those files.

**Existing incorrect result reproduced on both baseline and documented revision:**
`CyclotomicGraph::require_order` computes an unchecked u64 LCM before applying
its order cap. With optimized overflow checks disabled, the exact query
`sin(pi/(2^62+1))` admits wrapped order four, returns `Some(0)`, and publishes a
zero sign. Its mathematical value is strictly positive because its angle lies
strictly between zero and pi. The repository release profile disables overflow
checks and matches this reproduction. With debug overflow checks, the query
`sin(pi/(2^63-1))` instead panics in num-integer 0.1.46's LCM multiplication;
root facts remain invalid. A direct order-admission probe also reproduces that
panic. These are incorrect/panicking outcomes, not controlled exhaustion or
successful exact conformance. The existing nine tests do not cover them.

The query, graph-admission and order-admission documentation now records this
limitation. Runtime behavior remains unchanged under this docs-only session.
A future implementation change must bound/check the LCM before multiplication,
preserve both original hard cases as regressions, and verify debug and release
publication behavior. A doc correction does not repair the false certificate.

Other reviewed contracts and limitations:

- Numerator bounds separately track an integrality denominator and a uniform
  bound over complex embeddings. Quotient denominator factors are reciprocal
  operand numerators with nonzero obligations, not that integrality denominator.
  Zero certification tests every conjugate over distinct splitting primes until
  their product exceeds the numerator bound; one residue alone is insufficient.
  The first conjugate filter is repeated in the full conjugate pass.
- Allocation identity reuses live DAG nodes, without defining scalar equality.
  Postorder traversal preserves the existing stack/child order. Synthetic
  linear-combination instructions count toward the 4096-node cap. Node, field,
  coefficient and modular-work caps are distinct; graph admission, nested
  recognizers, bound arithmetic and allocations are not fully covered by the
  modular counter. No total memory/time bound is claimed.
- Rational-root recognition accepts the supported extracted residuals 1,2,3,6;
  this is a sufficient, representation-sensitive recognizer. Field inverses
  carry factor multisets rather than dividing residues directly. An inverse
  without a witnessed nonzero numerator declines. A rational coefficient whose
  denominator is divisible by the first selected prime also declines immediately,
  rather than trying another prime, even when the queried expression is zero.
- Primitive-root search tries bases 2 through 65; an unsuccessful first modulus
  can stop the attempt. The nested factor-residue options distinguish failure,
  an empty multiplicative identity, and a materialized residue vector. Modular
  zip assumes equal widths and otherwise truncates; addition/subtraction require
  normalized residues and the admitted prime range. Small-order trial factoring
  is not a general overflow-safe u64 factorization API.
- Successful ordinary certification publishes an exact zero sign without a
  retained field tower or numerical sample. Unsupported, cancelled or incomplete
  attempts do not publish negative evidence. The overflow defect above is an
  explicit exception to the intended publication guarantee. Existing fixtures
  cover nonzero perturbations, unsupported zero expressions, inverse-domain
  failure, cancellation/retry, sharing and admission caps with their original
  assertions unchanged.
- The old comment confused the twelve- and thirteen-base Miller–Rabin thresholds.
  The documented twelve-base threshold is 318665857834031151167461, already
  above all u64 values; the runtime bases are unchanged. The exact thresholds
  were checked against Theorem 1.1 of
  [Sorenson and Webster's primary paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1509.00864v1).

Temporary private probes ran against both baseline and final source. Independent
trial division agreed on primality for 20,000 integers; independent gcd counting
agreed on 1024 totients; 9458 modular operand pairs agreed with elementary
arithmetic. Sixteen denominator exponent cases checked pointwise maximum,
missing-factor and additive-product rules, including checked u32 exponent
exhaustion. A valid zero with the first splitting prime in its rational
coefficient denominator reproduced the documented normal decline. Separate
contained debug and optimized probes reproduced the two LCM defects above.
The probes used a 1 GiB address-space limit, ten CPU seconds and fifteen wall
seconds with core dumps disabled; these are diagnostic containment limits, not
production resource guarantees. This finite arithmetic evidence does not prove
universal field correctness, and does not override the incorrect release result.

The documentation now distinguishes:

- Raw node construction bypasses normalization and starts without bound/sign
  facts or a signal. Tags are not domain or range certificates. IntegralAtan(n)
  means atan(1/n), and AcosNegativeRational(r) means acos(-r) with nonnegative r.
  The zero-denominator fixture is used only to check argument-reader refusal.
- The 2048-bit MPFR oracles round rational inputs and function outputs outward.
  Increasing asinh, atan and atanh use corresponding lower/upper input endpoints;
  decreasing acos reverses them. Symbolic atan fixtures apply outward sqrt,
  exact binary scaling, outward atan, and endpoint-swapping negation. Rug converts
  finite endpoints to exact rationals. Atanh additionally requires its rounded
  input endpoints to remain inside (-1,1), as these fixtures ensure.
- Each enclosure helper interprets the returned integer a as a*2^p and requires
  the closed interval with radius 2^p to contain the entire MPFR interval. This
  is stronger than interval overlap but is not a correct-rounding assertion.
  Cold and warm samples need not be identical. Fixture shifts must fit signed
  precision arithmetic; arbitrary precision/resource safety is not established.
- Asinh checks 23 rational inputs through two tags at eight requests. Acos
  checks 12 magnitudes through imported and public construction at 13 requests.
  Atanh checks 25 interior inputs at 12 requests, approaching but never using
  the undefined ±1 endpoints. Integral atan checks ten signed denominators at
  13 requests. Generic atan checks 25 signed rational values through direct and
  raw Add(q,0) children at nine requests, plus 24 signed/scaled square-root
  inputs at seven requests. No dispatch-count assertion was added or inferred.
- Each boundary-rounding fixture enumerates all admissible integer samples for
  its selected finite input grid near ±1/2. Five precision pairs, 17 quarter-unit
  perturbations and both signs give 390 admitted samples and 1170 enclosure
  assertions after fine/coarse reuse. Asinh includes the coarse p=1 request;
  atan uses a finer -1024 follow-up. This finite exhaustiveness is not a claim
  about every real input or precision.
- Cancellation fixtures set the signal before entry, discard the returned abort
  integer, require the queried cache to remain empty, clear the flag, then check
  retry and an independent enclosure. The equality comparison is to the now-warm
  call; it does not certify abort placeholders, all child caches, or interruption
  at every internal stage. Concurrency cases are finite scoped schedules. In
  the facts fixture, a reader that makes no explicit warming request can still
  observe another thread's sample; it is not guaranteed a cold execution.
- Exact retained-argument fixtures check signed reciprocal recovery, unchanged
  family/payload and an unsampled original angle. For nonzero n, their square
  expectations are 1/(n²+1) and n²/(n²+1), with branch-aware signs. Pi shifts
  negate both coordinates; ±pi/2-minus-angle complements swap squares and set
  the expected signs. sign_until(0) must prove the square residual zero; the
  helper alone does not assert a particular proof path or absence of child work.
  Strict monotonicity gives atan(1/2)>atan(1/5).

An independent Python Fraction check enumerated every integer in each exact
allowed sample interval, rather than trusting the fixture's three-candidate
construction. It confirmed both 390/1170 counts and the selected working
precision pairs using integer logarithm bounds. Separate rational tangent
normalization and quarter-turn/reflection matrices confirmed 40 exact square
and sign rows for the ten denominators. These finite expectations supplement
the existing directed-MPFR tests; they do not constitute a universal kernel proof.

The documented contracts now make these distinctions explicit:

- PiAtanLinearForm and PiAcosLinearForm retain one recognized inverse-angle
  argument with rational offset/pi/function coefficients. Zero coefficients may
  retain an argument; distinct arguments can decline even with zero multipliers.
  PiAtanTermsForm separately keeps a list for sign/order reasoning. Scaling can
  leave zero list coefficients, while addition prunes them. These are recognizers,
  not transcendence bases or general angle-addition algorithms.
- Acos complements require nonnegative exact rational arguments a,b satisfying
  a²+b²=1 before substituting acos(b)=pi/2-acos(a). The sign requirements select
  the principal branches. Quarter-turn extraction requires zero offset, atan
  multiplier ±1 and a half-integer pi coefficient; its tuple identifies the
  coordinate swap and the signs multiplying the original atan coordinates.
- RadicalCoefficient retains a rational summand, partially reduced principal
  rational roots and structurally matched opaque atoms. Distinct radicals need
  not be algebraically independent. Eight radical entries are admitted, but
  opaque atoms have no local count cap. Rational scaling of atoms is supported;
  atom*atom and atom*radical products decline. A reciprocal requires a nonzero
  rational or a recognized single-radical conjugate norm. A zero norm alone is
  not a universal proof that the original value is zero.
- Laurent powers are sorted distinct i16 values, capped at eight entries, with
  checked addition/negation of exponents. Empty storage denotes scalar zero.
  Intermediate insertion limits can decline before a later cancellation; this
  is a representation restriction, not undefined arithmetic. Failed single
  insertions leave the receiver unchanged. The one-right-term multiplication
  path consumes left coefficients while preserving the existing insertion order.
- A query starts with a depth budget and 512 charged visits. Allocation-keyed
  shared-node memo hits precede depth/work checks. Mathematical equality alone
  does not create a memo hit. Unsupported expansion, including some exhausted
  descendants, can remain an exact opaque atom, so Some(polynomial) need not
  permit rational projection or reconstruction. Coefficient arithmetic, structural
  comparisons, allocation, memory and cancellation are not fully accounted by
  these counters. There is no total-resource guarantee or signal poll here.
- Rational projection accepts only empty or power-zero purely rational forms,
  retaining their exact sign on the shared root without rewriting the source or
  caching the rational value in this method. Compaction uses depth 64, refuses
  surviving atoms, reconstructs exact root/pi arithmetic and carries the already
  valid root sign and outer abort signal. An asserted signal does not prevent
  this purely symbolic work. No numerical approximation is required.
- Fixture docs distinguish scalar interpolation from a geometric pcurve, and
  same-process JSON replay from fresh-process replay. The 38 direct quarter-turn
  cases use exact 3-4-5 coordinates. The diagonal case checks signs and squared
  values 49/50 and 1/50, not rational leaf representation. Refusal fixtures retain
  their 10^-12 perturbations and extra angle terms. The local compaction fixture
  checks admission/root cache state; separate existing consumers check equality,
  repeated compaction, signs and signal retention.

conjugate inverses against rational expectations and their identity product,

overflow, complementary acos branches and shared-node accounting. An initial

The documentation now records:

- Shared-factor extraction peels negation and binary scaling but only recognizes
  a direct constant or a product with a direct constant child. It does not search
  nested products/sums. A returned child carries its own signal; newly built
  wrappers need not carry the outer signal or become rational leaves. Defined
  source operands are required. Wrapper recursion has no explicit depth/work cap.

  and arithmetic precedence. Their budget limits recursive depth, not aggregate
  visits, coefficient size, allocation or nested helper work. Products prefer
  the left exact-rational scale. None does not establish invalidity or inequality.
  These paths do not poll cancellation or numerically refine.
- The unsigned half-pi reader recognizes orientation*pi/2-atan(x) at depth 32.
  Its signed counterpart additionally requires sign(x)=orientation, proving the
  principal identity atan(1/x). The acos-shift reader instead returns the
  coefficient orientation in orientation*(acos(x)-pi/2), not the angle's sign,
  and imposes no corresponding argument-sign requirement.

  the original atan coordinates. Diagonal tuples give signs of the rotation's
  sine/cosine components (each magnitude 1/sqrt(2)) and of the atan multiplier;
  they are not signs of the final coordinates. Only odd pi/4 turns qualify.

  form construction, not on failed later projection of an already recognized
  form. Pure-pi recovery is explicitly opt-in through the finite anchor table;
  the Real-facing quarter-turn entry keeps it disabled. A retained argument with
  zero coefficient is not treated as the no-argument pure-pi case.
- Atan-to-acos conversion admits rational or pure-quadratic tangents only when
  sqrt(t²/(1+t²)) is exactly rational, preserving the principal branch and using
  positive orientation at t=0. A recognized atan that fails conversion returns
  immediately. Asin and negative-rational acos use their exact reflected formulas;
  original real domains must already be admitted. Laurent projection admits only
  the required rational powers and convertible atoms, not arbitrary radicals.
- Sign rules use atan monotonicity, coefficient/argument signs and strict principal
  range bounds. For a nonzero pi coefficient, 2*abs(pi_coefficient) at least the
  sum of absolute atan coefficients gives a strict sign because finite atan values
  are strictly inside (-pi/2,pi/2). Acos rules use its principal nonnegative range,
  the x=1 endpoint and half-pi shifts; that endpoint check alone is not full domain
  validation. Some missing required argument signs return early. Nested helpers
  may reuse/retain facts, while this method does not itself publish the root sign.
- Retained pi-multiple reading declines pure rational zero; Laurent projection
  admits the empty form as zero. Structural depth and Laurent node accounting
  remain distinct. Sine-term recognition requires a stored PrescaledSin argument
  r*pi with 0<r<1/2, not an arbitrary periodic or cosine representation. The open
  range 0<sin(pi*r)<1 proves strict signs even at zero interval endpoints; an
  interval crossing zero can decline despite the actual scalar having a definite
  sign. Addition may retain the proof returned by this bound.

Ownership is Hyperreal's exact native construction and scalar evaluation boundary,
P1–P7, with cached facts and downstream predicate consumers under P8–P11 and
retained composition under P19–P20. The missing witness was faithful documentation
of actual constructor rewrites, admitted input domains, metadata/signal behavior,

The documentation now distinguishes:

- Native infallible arithmetic requires already-defined operands, and inverse
  requires nonzero input. Recognized cancellation and zero annihilation can discard
  other subgraphs without validating their domains. Constructors are not universal
  import validators or replacements for checked Real entry points.
- Negation, inversion, square, multiplication and addition preserve their existing
  rewrite/predicate sequence. Nonzero/nonnegative guards protect the selected
  reciprocal/square-root rewrites. Generic nodes carry only their established
  sign/bound facts; identities and reconstructed nodes need not share one storage
  shape, cache state or signal attachment.
- General multiplication recognizes binary scales before general rational-product
  folding, while multiply_rational folds a rational self first. Thus 2*3 can be an
  Offset through multiply and a rational leaf through multiply_rational, both
  exactly six. Shift-left retains nested offsets when checked exponent addition
  fails, and square/inverse retain their outer node when exponent movement fails.
  Those construction guards do not certify safe arbitrary-precision evaluation.
- Rational affine-offset recognition charges one shared traversal unit per call.
  Eight-visit callers do not receive a total arithmetic/work budget. Binary shifts
  are limited to absolute value 4096 and individual rational scales to 4097 bits;
  direct rational offsets and accumulated coefficients are not covered by those
  individual checks. Failed branches retain their spent budget. The two local
  equality helpers are sufficient cancellation recognizers, not complete equality
  procedures; commuted-pair checks do not generally reorder sums.
- The three-term retained dot stores ordered computable coefficients and rational
  weights, avoiding a separate product/sum graph per term. It starts with invalid
  facts and no signal. Its kernel can skip zero-weight children and has separate
  representable-magnitude/precision prerequisites, not a general domain or resource
  guarantee. The current out-of-range weight limitation remains described in the
  separately reviewed kernel docs.
- A new arithmetic wrapper commonly has no outer abort attachment, while identity
  returns can keep the chosen operand's signal. Even rational scaling by one can
  rebuild an exact rational leaf first and drop its attachment. abort changes only
  that wrapper's attachment: previous clones retain their old attachment, later
  clones share the new Arc, child attachments/caches are not recursively modified,
  and explicit approx_signal inputs override it for that request. Setting a flag
  is not a synchronous cancellation receipt.
- Erf uses an auxiliary series multiplied by exp(-x²) and 2/sqrt(pi); erfc, erfcx,
  CDF, density and their logarithms retain the actual exact compositions. Some
  composite constructors can refine through exponential range selection, so they
  are not uniformly lazy. Erfc/log-tail wrappers are not separate tail asymptotic
  algorithms. Positive/negative initial facts presume defined finite input.
- normal_interval is the signed difference Phi(hi)-Phi(lo), not unconditional
  nonnegative probability mass. It permits reversed endpoints, checks structural
  equality first, then evaluates both depth-48 rational projections in lower/upper
  order even if the first declines. Their sign facts may be retained. Exact order
  supplies the result sign; uncertain order stays unproved. Quantile seeds remain
  evaluation hints, with interior probability admission required and exact CDF
  inverse facts preferred. No new practical input window, total-work or heap-byte
  budget is introduced by these constructors.

Temporary probes on baseline and documented source checked 49 rational operand
pairs against exact sum/product expectations, unary identities, the two distinct
storage paths for six, clone/identity/rebuild signal cases, checked extreme-offset
fallbacks, a retained dot with exact value 2*7+3*11+5*13=112, shared affine traversal
charges, the 4096/4097 shift boundary, the 4097/4098 scale-bit boundary, an admitted
8193-bit direct offset, normal interval signs, exact zero-input function values
and the half-probability quantile shortcut with an attached signal and extreme seed
exponent. These finite probes are not complete algebra or resource proofs.

**Existing invalid/overflow behavior reproduced separately from valid arithmetic:**
Computable::zero().inverse() retains an Inverse node; approx(0) returns and caches
zero instead of a typed domain error. Zero multiplication/scaling and direct
self-cancellation can discard that invalid subgraph. These are violations of a
putative checked-input contract, not successful reciprocal/cancellation proofs;
valid-domain native callers must not supply the invalid operand. Debug
shift_right(i32::MIN) panics on negation. The retained ErfSeries at x=65536,p=0
panics in its magnitude guard; this is an evaluation implementation limit even
though erf is mathematically defined there. Both panics were caught in contained
probes, and neither is typed exhaustion. Runtime behavior is unchanged in this
docs-only session. Constructor docs describe the limitations rather than claiming
that documentation repairs them.

Documented and reconciled 91 blocks: five file overviews, eight module facades,
five structs, two enums, six variants, 21 named and two tuple fields, twelve
functions, three test functions, three impl blocks, twenty methods, one module
constant and three function-local constants. Private/test Rustdoc contains 88
blocks; the three local constants require supplemental rendered Markdown because
Rustdoc does not expose body-local items. Inspected all eleven derived trait
anchors: Input Clone/Debug/Deserialize/Serialize, Recipe Clone/Debug/Serialize,
and OffsetFamily Clone/Copy/Debug/Serialize. Serde shape validation, unknown-field
rejection, absent Recipe deserialization and public-field mutation obligations
are documented. The inventory initially counted multiline function parameters
as fields; restricting its field scan to struct bodies resolved that scratch
script error without changing any source or coverage requirement.

The benchmark measures one request per process. The external runner owns sample
ordering, affinity and timeout. Timed work includes backend construction,
materialized rational endpoints, width checks and retained intermediate steps;
recipe decoding, target construction, private-class inspection, fixed reference,
JSON encoding and final step disposal are outside the timer. Hyperreal reuses
one Real across stages, while MPFR reconstructs its expression at each precision.
Both can warm constant caches. The fifteen settings 256, 384, ..., 2048 denote
absolute dyadic precision magnitudes for Hyperreal but significand bits for MPFR.
They limit requests/stages, not total work, memory or cancellation. The file-size
check observes metadata before an uncapped read; it is not a hard read bound.

checked_steps verifies ordered intervals, reference overlap and first-sufficient
width. It does not verify containment of the exact value, interval nesting,
precision labels or recipe class. run and the external competitive validator
perform their separate checks. The fixed reference avoids Hyperreal evaluation,
but uses the same MPFR backend and corresponding formulas as the variable adapter;
agreement of those two paths is not independent evidence about MPFR or recipe
interpretation. Directed arithmetic relies on valid ordered finite inputs and
monotone generated domains. Sign extraction assumes ordered bounds and cannot
certify zero. Invariant panics are not converted to error JSON. Cache cleanup
runs after normal return, not after an uncaught panic.

Recipe documentation preserves correlated byte uses, signed exact scaling, prime
and angle selection, pi powers, four positive inner offset families and all
78 decimal cancellation depths. Requested labels are not proof of private class.
The exact wire encoder includes /1 for integers and avoids mixed-number Display.
The benchmark fixture checks 22 labels times four genomes, but its class/kind
assertions apply to the inventory representatives; the downstream probe tests
separately check generated classes. Neither finite corpus establishes closure
for all exact scalar inputs.

Atlas kind labels are generator choices, not runtime class assertions. Source
bit widths can shrink through canonical reduction, and the irrational numerator
construction adds a magnitude bit. Rational setup occurs outside timing; scalar

proofs, and Problem categories are discarded by these adapters. Atlas's ceilings
and predictions can omit work and do not preempt calls. powi uses positive
power-of-two exponents, and the irrational sqrt row roots an already rooted input.

## Hyperreal shared benchmark-report implementation audit

Baseline: `6fb6c1b783628ae44ef4eda8bc2efc0cef88192a`. Read all 476 existing lines
of `crates/hyperreal/benches/support/benchmark_report.rs` (now 648), including
all private records/helpers and both tests. Read its direct example, nine
benchmark registration/wrapper consumers, current manifest and
scripts/bench-reports.sh as context; no whole-file credit is added for those
context reads. This closes the included-helper gap recorded by the example
facade audit, not the remaining benchmark implementations or repository audit.

Ownership is development evidence discovery/presentation under P36 and P37,
with explicit failure/resource behavior from P5/P6. The domain is stored
Criterion JSON, current simple explicit bench manifest declarations and marked
Markdown. Missing acceptance evidence was complete private-item Rustdoc that
states what the helper actually validates and what its counts mean. Baseline
example tests and a task-owned filesystem fixture were executed before edits.
No runtime implementation, emitted report string, test or fixture was changed;
raw non-comment tokens are identical to baseline.

Documented and checked 51 blocks: one module overview, five constants, three
structs, seventeen fields, twenty-two functions, one test module and two tests.
All descriptions/field anchors render in private/test-enabled documentation.
Reviewed the three derived Debug implementations and their rendered anchors;
they format stored fields without recomputing or validating evidence. No body-local
items or other authored macro-generated API require supplemental rendering here.

The callback ignores its Criterion argument and reads stored files. It honors
skip-variable presence, requires --bench and suppresses --test/--list/--help;
the direct writer bypasses that guard. It logs errors instead of propagating
them as benchmark failure. Directory resolution distinguishes CRITERION_HOME,
absolute/relative CARGO_TARGET_DIR, executable ancestors and fallback paths.
Shared directories can contain other crates' results. Neither provenance nor
successful execution of every declared target is validated.

Traversal treats directories named new as leaves, ignores nondirectories and
keeps usable rows in a BTreeMap by full_id. Repeated IDs replace earlier values
in filesystem iteration order; sorted output does not make duplicate selection
deterministic. Missing required fields omit rows, missing optional statistics
fall back to the mean, and malformed change data is ignored. Missing/non-u64
throughput counts become zero for a selected object entry. No positivity,
confidence-level, confidence-order or statistical-validity check is supplied;
the fixed 95% CI heading is not established by parsing. Comparison groups depend
on labels, not proof of equivalent completed work. The summary's comparisons
field counts participating rows, not groups.

Manifest discovery is a line/quote parser, not Cargo/TOML authority. It ignores
features before a name, uses guessed source paths, and classifies Criterion by
literal substrings even in comments. Report links are guessed and not checked.
Markdown escaping only handles pipes/backticks. Replacement touches the first
marker pair; later pairs survive, and a missing closing marker discards the tail
from the opening marker. Existing-report read errors, including invalid UTF-8,
fall back to a fresh heading before an unlocked non-atomic write. Recursion,
input allocation, retained rows and cancellation have no explicit total contract.
The docs preserve these limitations without fixing runtime behavior in this
session's docs-only worktree.

The existing replacement test checks a single marker and changed content, not
bytewise idempotence of repeating one replacement. The manifest test checks
fifteen entries, two selected names and a non-Criterion entry, not equivalence
to Cargo metadata. Both assertions remain intact.

The docs distinguish exact native expressions plus -112 requested enclosures
from nearest-rounded MPFR points. The Carlson reference is pi/(2 AGM(1,sqrt(y)))
for y=2^-bits, bits=1,20,128. Its expected point uses 1024-bit precision and its
timed point uses 256 bits. Other references use 1024-bit complete AGM or the
independent forward series, safeguarded inverse and derived Jacobi components.
Complete Legendre uses m=1/2,-3; incomplete uses (phi,m)=(3/4,1/2),(15/2,-3/4).
Both inverse kinds and Jacobi use (u,m)=(3/4,1/2),(3/4,-3/4),(7/2,1/2),
(-7/2,-3/4). Values are parsed from exact decimal input. The forward MPFR
closure computes both integral kinds before selecting one; inverse references
also evaluate both forward-series components. That work remains in timings.

Every mode, including MPFR, prepares and refines a native expression/triplet
before timing. Cold means fresh result construction inside the loop, not a
fresh process or cleared global caches. Warm clones retain prepared evidence.
The timer includes construction/cloning, evaluation, vector allocation and row
storage, plus native expression temporaries destroyed in the loop. Preparation,
validation, printing and destruction of retained rows occur afterward/outside.
Native rows retain enclosures, not the original expressions through validation.

Carlson validation compares the 1024-bit rounded expected point with nearest-
rounded endpoint conversions and checks exact rational width below 2^-96;
its MPFR points require strict absolute difference below 2^-96. Other native
checks contain the adopted exact binary rational of the reference and have
width below 2^-96. Their point checks require the -112 difference enclosure
inside inclusive +/-2^-96. Jacobi checks all three fixed-array components and
counts accepted triplets, not components. These finite checks do not turn a
rounded reference into a directed mathematical oracle. Repeating the same MPFR
formula/solver as the expectation is not an independent MPFR correctness proof.

All programs ignore arguments, emit JSON to stdout and do not write benchmark
Markdown. They print each row before asserting accepted==repeats; process success
and accepted counts are both required. Construction, reference and enclosure
failures panic rather than emitting typed benchmark outcomes. Fixed schedules
and precision requests add no total-work/memory/cancellation bound. No explicit
MPFR cache-cleanup guard is installed. The existing allow(dead_code) attribute
is unchanged; its inverse-benchmark comment now correctly notes that only complete
AGM is unused, because the sibling inverse also consumes conversions and series.

The raw timer takes the minimum of five sequential wall-clock calls, including
returned-value destruction. Reused inputs/global caches can warm between calls.
It does not inspect generic Result/Option outcomes, validate approximations or

includes setup/formatting/sorting and all nested clocks, not just scalar work.

Documented the 37 rational, 41 computable and 43 Real prepared-input catalogues;
their sizes were reproduced without running all collectors. Wide generation uses
nonzero signed rationals and binary exponents -96..96; the bounded generator lies
in -999..999, not necessarily the unit interval. Generated seeds/operands are
deterministic and correlated. TARGET_CASES bounds retained collection length,
not individual evaluation time or input-controlled allocation. The general
scaled helper's i32::MIN negation panics in the checked fixture, and fraction
helpers unwrap zero denominators. These existing behaviors were documented,
not changed in this docs-only session.

Report paths are cwd-relative, despite the crate_* helper names. Reads can turn
file errors into empty history. The simple pipe/backtick parser cannot reliably
read its own writer's pair inputs containing |; it also drops any line containing
Rank or --- even inside a field. Imported family/operation labels are leaked for
static lifetimes, including some rows later discarded by filtering/truncation.
Duration parsing accepts extra tokens, maps negatives/NaN to zero and positive
infinity/overflow to u128::MAX. Larger formatted durations use rounded f64 text.
History merges exact textual keys, retaining maxima of parsed historical values
and new probe minima, then caps 1,000 rows. This is not a complete worst-ever
record: rounding, parse failures and earlier truncation can discard evidence.

Promotion admits five named computable operations and limited rational text.
The parser does not verify a seed/value relationship, accepts signed mixed-number
fractions and loses the sign of -0. Zero denominators panic rather than returning
None. The fourth tab field is optional/ignored by this loader but required by the
companion consumer. Duplicates remain. Rotation reprobes with historical maxima,
releases the fastest retained-score row and excludes its key from immediate
reentry; sparse pools can shrink instead of reaching 100. Candidate order comes
from the caller. Generated names normalize text but are not collision-proof.

Current scoring uses fresh minima, not historical maxima, and can score any number
of eligible file rows, including duplicates. Its saturating u128 sum followed by
division can understate a mean. Prior metadata parsing is not section-scoped;
missing fields default, cases is synthesized as 100 and derivative as zero.
Delta and its change may compare different rosters/hardware/cache states. Source
inspection also discloses unchecked i128 casts/subtractions; extreme signed-score
overflow was not executed by this fixture. The score-loop's missing/empty-set None
becomes a timed zero sentinel, not successful completion of 100 cases.

Writers are unlocked/non-atomic and log errors without propagating failure.
The direct report writer updates the cwd promoted list before the supplied report
path, with no transaction or rollback. Only wrapper writes honor skip-variable
presence; collection/scoring can still run. Score text always says 100 offenders
but displays the actual supplied count. A missing closing marker prepends a new
section while retaining the malformed original; matched replacement keeps both
the new final newline and old suffix, so repeated updates can add blank lines.
No escaping/general Markdown parser or bytewise idempotence is promised.

  randomized fuzzing or complete numerical-domain coverage. The eight fixed
  candidates include negative 2^512 and negative 2^-512.
- File loading uses the current directory, requires four tab-separated fields,
  ignores timing text and does not validate seed text. Any nonempty accepted
  list replaces the fallback without backfill or a 100-case limit. Empty names
  and duplicates survive; names leak before operation/input rejection. The
  companion history reader's three-field rows are not accepted by this loader.
- Word-sized parsing rejects negative mixed fractional numerators and decimals,
  loses the sign of textual negative zero, and can panic on zero denominators
  or an oversized mixed numerator. The minimum signed exponent also panics in
  the scaling helper; large shifts have no local allocation/work budget. These
  existing defects and limitations remain unchanged for implementation work.
- The historical ln_abs_plus_one operation actually constructs ln(x*x+1).
  Batched helpers exclude prepared-source cloning and returned-output drops
  from timing; whole-vector sweeps include cloning and result destruction.
  Clones retain shared caches. The separate promoted log in the inverse-trig
  group is prebuilt before registration and can reuse its own numeric cache.
  Catalogue claims of cold work are not guarantees. Criterion durations and
  approximation precision are not hard bounds on elapsed work or memory.
- Most results, including fallible shortcut results, are merely black-boxed.
  Only atanh(1) requires an error and does not check its variant. The workload
  supplies no independent numerical oracle, general cancellation check or
  correctness/performance regression assertion. Successful smoke execution is
  not certification of the represented mathematical results or timing evidence.

Documented behavior and limits:

  not invalidate arithmetic caches. Recording does not aggregate other threads.
  The snapshot is retained only when raw dispatch labels are nonempty: rational
  statistics alone do not preserve a row. A nonempty repeated name replaces its
  old entry, but an empty repeated sample does not remove the old entry. Printed
  path counts measure distinct label tuples, not summed event multiplicity.

  collect_rows still prepares cached sign fixtures and final adversarial sources
  outside filtering. Full-run and subset cache histories differ. The exp-cached
  row includes its own initial approximation inside the trace, whereas several
  cached-sign rows warm before recording. Map/report order is lexical; execution
  order remains source order. Names such as unknown, unsupported, fallback and
  inconclusive do not assert present-day algorithmic outcomes.

  exact binary values. Mixed-number sign handling, zero-denominator/oversized
  numerator failures, root-domain unwraps and nonfinite-import panics are stated.
  Chain helpers document their formulas, construction counts and unconditional
  warmup in the perturbed case. Native simplification can change graph shape;
  construction depth and approximation/sign floors are not total-work limits.
  The three nested zero-identity helpers state their actual root expressions,
  without claiming that black-boxed sign results prove the identities.
- The report projects full snapshots to correlation counts and raw dispatch
  tuples, omitting some detailed rational statistics. It does not escape labels,
  lock or atomically replace the file. Output is cwd-relative and can replace a
  full report with an empty/subset one. Presence of the skip environment variable
  suppresses writing even when its value is empty. I/O errors are logged and
  swallowed; main still prints an unconditional updated message after a skipped
  or failed write. These existing limitations remain unchanged.
- Results are diagnostic. Most fallible operations unwrap; sign/comparison/
  approximation results and counts have no expected-value assertions here.
  The runner provides no independent correctness oracle, total-resource bound,
  cancellation handler or performance measurement.

  inside its timed closure, while most transcendental batched rows construct

  ordinary iteration; callback-level setup can run with row filters applied.

  from retained graph nodes. Identity multiplication can collapse; add depth
  5000 represents 5001. Structural-bound iteration is x -> 8/(7*x), alternating
  pi and 8/(7*pi). Scaled and half-square chains raise their initial scaled pi
  to 2^depth, which can grow rapidly. Inverse pairs and negate-square-root
  chains retain pi; sqrt-square chains retain two. Several helpers explicitly
  warm their source even at depth zero. No helper adds a total resource budget.

  input means its binary value. Named algebraic cancellation fixtures state
  their actual root formulas and unwrap failures. Native inverse-function
  adapters add no domain validation or typed errors, and retain their native
  resource and construction-evaluation behavior.

  comparing magnitudes. A tolerance-based Equal result need not prove exact
  equality. The comparison rows black-box optional orders and toleranced orders
  without assertions. Interval rows similarly black-box Option results without
  requiring Some; zero-identity names do not assert a certified zero result.
- Three pre-registration checks require coarse exp(3/2) at precision 1 to yield
  integer 2 or 3, coarse expm1(3/2) to yield 1 or 2, and exp(-10000) at -128 to

  half, not by two. Two exp-half/near-limit rows both use exact one-half; ln
  near-limit uses 47/32, near-pole tangent uses pi/2-1/64, and huge trig uses
  2^512*pi+7/5. Names alone do not enforce thresholds or a regression policy.

  row builds (1+10^-7)*(1-10^-7)-1 inside ordinary timing. Gaussian interval

Documented and reproduced findings:

- Five borrowed GMP rational arithmetic forms return incomplete expression
  objects. The local timing macro black-boxes and drops them without completing
  arithmetic, whereas native operations return completed Rational values.
  Integer magnitude rows explicitly complete the GMP operations and therefore
  have a different workload. Pair labels alone do not establish equal work.
- MPFR sinc_pi divides sin(pi*x) by x instead of pi*x; cosc divides 1-cos(x)
  by x instead of x squared; lower inverse Mills computes CDF/PDF instead of
  PDF/CDF. At the actual fixed inputs (3/4, 3/4 and zero), native-minus-reference
  enclosures at precision -80 exclude the entire interval [-1/100,1/100]. The
  adopted references are exact rational values of the rounded MPFR points.
- The rational binary64 row pairs optional exact dyadic conversion with rounded
  conversion; 355/113 yields None on the exact side and a finite rounded value.
  The alleged enclosure helper rounds to directed 53-bit MPFR endpoints but
  converts them to binary64 using nearest rounding. Positive 2^-1075 gives
  [0,0], and finite 2^1024 gives [infinity,infinity], neither an enclosure.
  The ordinary 355/113 endpoints do enclose the input.
- The GMP perfect-power partner checks numerator and denominator independently,
  without a shared exponent. It accepts 16/27 while the native rational
  predicate rejects it. Square-extraction rows also expose different output
  contracts: factor/residual versus integer square roots/remainders.
- General Real rows mostly construct exact expressions; MPFR partners compute
  rounded points. Computable absolute precision -128 differs from MPFR's
  128-bit significand precision. Selected elliptic/inverse rows force native
  rational intervals and check rounded reference discrepancies at -144 against
  inclusive +/-2^-124 before timing. Reference working precision varies among
  128, 256 and 1024 bits. These finite checks are not directed MPFR enclosures
  or a general same-contract speed comparison. Prechecks also warm state.
- Rounded Gaussian/gamma/beta/moment helpers add no general validation or typed
  convergence contract. Inverse erf always performs eight Newton updates;
  inverse isometric latitude uses 160 rounded bisections at 256 bits and returns
  a 128-bit midpoint without a bracket, residual or rounding proof. Binomial
  multiplication can overflow before division: debug probes panic at (3,4) and
  (67,33), the latter despite the final mathematical coefficient fitting u64.
  Integer beta arithmetic can overflow, and moment powers narrow usize to u32.
- Prepared inputs/constants and shared caches may survive calls. Ordinary iter
  includes spelled-out clones/constructions and output destruction. Most rows
  only black-box results; no general cross-backend equivalence or output check
  is performed. There is no explicit MPFR cache-cleanup hook, total work bound
  or allocation bound in this runner. These limits are described per helper
  and group, without changing the benchmark or claiming performance evidence.

Reviewed every line of three baseline files at
be5b87736: rational/arithmetic/toom4_multiplication.rs (138 lines),
toom6_multiplication.rs (143 lines), and toom8_multiplication.rs (104 lines),

The owning layer is Hyperreal's exact nonnegative magnitude arithmetic. Relevant
properties are P1 (exact reconstruction), P4/P10 (unchanged ordered dispatch and
trace effects), P5 (unbounded intermediate work/memory), P6 (invariant failure
versus typed outcomes), and the public/private Rustdoc mandate. The missing
acceptance witness was accurate documentation of all private helpers, mathematical
interpolation invariants, resource limits and benchmark API visibility. Before
editing, nine existing all-feature Toom tests and strict private rustdoc passed;
the generated Rational page omitted all four doc(hidden) benchmark methods.

Added or replaced 27 authored blocks: three inherent impl descriptions, four
associated constants and twenty methods. Removed doc(hidden) from the production
selector benchmark wrapper and three forced-family candidates. Their signatures
and visibility were already public; only documentation visibility changed.
Noncomment tokens match after excluding those four documentation attributes.
No predicate order, selector threshold, interpolation weight, assert, trace,
arithmetic expression or runtime behavior was changed. Existing include-fragment
expression formatting was preserved instead of reformatting the large tables.

Documented mathematical/operational contracts:

- Each kernel splits magnitudes into n base-B chunks, B=2^ceil(max_bits/n),
  evaluates degree-(n-1) polynomials and reconstructs a degree-(2n-2) product.
  Toom-4/6/8 use 7/11/15 point products respectively; scalar-weight products
  and recombination are additional work. Point products use the integer backend,
  not recursive calls to Hyperreal's selector. Shifted addition preserves carries
  even when recovered coefficients exceed one base-B digit.
- End coefficients come directly from chunk products; finite-point values have
  those contributions removed. The static inverse Vandermonde weights recover
  the middle coefficients exactly. Direct integer convolution explains their
  nonnegativity. The independent audit checks all 275 inverse-matrix identities
  with Python Fraction arithmetic, covering every table row and basis power.
  This establishes the interpolation identities, not an unrestricted resource
  guarantee or complete implementation proof.
- Selection order is Toom-8, Toom-6, Toom-4, backend. Shorter-operand thresholds
  are 262144, 524288 and 1048576 bits, with longer <= shorter+floor(shorter/n)
  and saturating upper-bound addition. Gates overlap; earlier eligible families
  win. Zero operands fail the gates and reach the backend, whereas direct kernels
  return zero before splitting. Candidates bypass gates and record their path
  before that zero return when tracing is active.
- Chunk extraction retains only n windows and returns zeros at width zero;
  multiplication's positive ceiling width makes its own extraction lossless.
  Arbitrary signed coefficient arrays can be evaluated by Horner's rule. Linear
  combination helpers require nonzero divisors and valid exactly divisible
  interpolation data. Remainders are always computed; nonzero remainders panic
  only with debug assertions, while release division truncates toward zero.
  A zero divisor panics. Negative recovered coefficients also panic.
- These functions return fully materialized BigUints. Signs, denominator
  cancellation and rational normalization belong to their consumers. No retained
  recipe, cache, precision budget, total-work/memory bound, cancellation or typed
  resource-exhaustion result is added here. Thresholds are tuning gates, not
  mathematical validity limits or resource contracts. No performance claim is
  inferred from the names, thresholds or finite qualification corpus.

Reviewed every line of the 212-line baseline
crates/hyperreal/src/rational/arithmetic/ntt_multiplication.rs at 5b5c23b63.

The owning layer is Hyperreal's exact integer magnitude benchmark candidate.
Relevant properties are P1 (exact modular reconstruction), P5 (transform capacity
versus total resources), P6 (panic guards rather than typed outcomes), and the
public/private Rustdoc mandate. Missing acceptance was documentation of every
helper's preconditions, actual resource handling and visible benchmark API.

omitted the existing doc(hidden) candidate method; source review confirms that
this candidate is called directly by benchmarks/tests rather than selected by
