Added or replaced eleven authored Rustdoc blocks: one inherent impl, three
constants and seven methods. Removed doc(hidden) from the already-public NTT
benchmark method so its reviewed contract appears in ordinary Rustdoc. Corrected
two adjacent ordinary comment lines in the GMP coverage catalogue: magnitude
probes are classified separately from the rational API, rather than all being
hidden. No catalogue entry, fixture or test changed. Noncomment tokens match
before/after after excluding the single documentation attribute; all runtime
arithmetic, trace calls and precondition checks are unchanged. Existing include-
fragment formatting is retained.

Documented contracts and independently checked mathematics:

- Little-endian base-32768 digits become zero-padded modular convolutions. The
  primes are 2013265921=15*2^27+1 and 998244353=119*2^23+1, with primitive
  roots 31 and 3. Trial division verifies primality; factor/order checks verify
  the roots, including every power-of-two transform length from 1 through 2^23.
  Reduced residue products fit u64. Forward transforms use positive root powers;
  inverse transforms use reciprocal stage roots and inverse-length scaling.
- The transform helper requires a nonempty power-of-two length dividing p-1,
  valid prime/root data and reduced residues for its mathematical transform
  contract. It does not validate those preconditions; an empty slice is a no-op
  with valid moduli. Convolution allocates two residue buffers, retains padded
  output and is cyclic unless length covers the full linear coefficient count.
  Too-short input buffers panic while slicing.
- For digit lengths a,b, coefficient_count=a+b-1 and the next power of two must
  be <=2^23. The coefficient bound is 32767^2*min(a,b); the admitted length
  implies min(a,b)<=4194304 and a bound of 4503324753657856, below the prime
  product 2009731336725594113. CRT therefore uniquely recovers each nonnegative
  convolution coefficient, and exact carry propagation reconstructs the integer.
  These arithmetic checks establish the documented bounds, not a measured peak-
  memory or universal completion claim.
- Zero operands return zero before conversion. Otherwise input digit vectors
  are allocated before length/CRT assertions. Length arithmetic and conversions
  can panic or overflow; transform-capacity and CRT failure are panics rather
  than typed exhaustion. The first residue vector remains live during the
  second convolution. No total-work/memory accounting or cancellation exists.
  Maximum-capacity and oversized allocation workloads were not run in this
  documentation batch.
- Digit extraction strips high zeros; zero has no digits. Packing requires
  digits below 32768 and uses OR without range validation: invalid [32768,1]
  packs to 32768 rather than the carry-expanded 65536. Modular powering does
  not initially reduce its base and returns literal one at exponent zero,
  including modulus zero/one. Positive-exponent modulus zero panics; oversized
  bases can overflow before reduction. Current NTT calls satisfy the intended
  bounds. The wrapper records its trace before the zero fast path when recording
  is active; the private kernel adds no trace event.

## Hyperreal Barrett division documentation batch

Reviewed every line of the 129-line baseline
crates/hyperreal/src/rational/arithmetic/barrett_division.rs at 890362e2c.
The final file has 203 lines. This covers every stored field, derived role,
preparation/fallback branch, block operation, assertion, trace and batch loop.
Context review included its include host, the already-audited scalar benchmark,
three existing unit tests and the existing GMP public-name classification.
Those reads do not credit the larger unit-test, catalogue or include-host files
as newly whole-file reviewed.

The owning layer is Hyperreal's exact unsigned division benchmark machinery.
Relevant properties are P1 (exact quotient/remainder and reciprocal invariants),
P4/P10 (preserved execution/tracing), P5 (unbounded work/memory), P6 (invalid
input panics versus eligibility outcomes), and private/public Rustdoc coverage.
Missing acceptance was accurate documentation of every private field/helper and
of the already-public benchmark methods. Before editing, all three all-feature
Barrett tests passed and the public docs omitted the three doc(hidden) methods.

Added or replaced thirteen authored blocks: one struct, four fields, two impl
blocks and six methods. Reviewed the derived Clone/Debug behavior and documented
its relation to owned BigUint storage; both generated impl anchors render in
private docs. Removed doc(hidden) from the one-shot candidate, batch candidate
and backend-batch comparator. Signatures and Rust visibility were already public;
only documentation visibility changed. Runtime tokens are identical after
excluding those three attributes. No threshold, correction loop, assertion,
trace event, fixture or call order changed; include-fragment formatting remains
as authored.

Documented findings and mathematical reasoning:

- Preparation stores d, k=bits(d), B-1 for B=2^k and the exact truncated
  reciprocal mu=floor(B^2/d). It returns None for d=0, d=1 or failed bit-width
  conversion. The wrappers reject zero first and fall back to the backend when
  preparation declines, notably for one. Saturating 2*k arithmetic is not work
  or memory admission; allocation/representable-shift requirements remain.
- A valid combined block x<d*B is estimated by
  q0=floor(floor(x/2^(k-1))*mu/2^(k+1)). Both truncations round down, so q0
  cannot exceed floor(x/d). Reciprocal truncation loses less than one quotient
  unit and prefix truncation less than 2^(k-1)/d<=1; therefore the integer
  estimate is at most two low. Corrections recover q,r exactly. The range,
  nonnegative subtraction and correction bound are debug assertions, not a
  hard release iteration limit or typed validation of arbitrary forged state.
- Multi-block division keeps r<d and forms x=r*B+digit<d*B, so the quotient
  digit fits k bits. Iterating high-to-low materializes q and r satisfying
  dividend=q*d+r and 0<=r<d. Dividend<d returns zero plus a cloned dividend.
  There is no shared global reciprocal cache or retained cross-call result.
- One-shot preparation occurs even for a zero/small dividend when d>=2. Batch
  preparation occurs before iteration, even for an empty batch, and is reused
  only within that call. Both batch methods reject zero even with no dividends;
  successful output retains input order. Neither batch emits the one-shot
  division-candidate event.
- The one-shot event precedes preparation, including divisor-one fallback;
  its block-wise-barrett label identifies the requested wrapper, not proof of
  the actual prepared kernel. Zero rejection precedes that event. Results
  are exact BigUint pairs but resource limits, cancellation and typed exhaustion
  are absent. The prepared fields must remain mutually coherent; Clone copies
  their owned values and Debug reports them without recomputing the reciprocal.

The owning layer is Hyperreal's scalar diagnostic classification, with one exact

(preserved predicate order and tracing), P5/P6 (unbounded backend work and invalid

Reproduced diagnostic limitations:

- Multiplication counts original native-word limbs, sorts their lengths, then
  chooses basecase at shorter<=32; half-Karatsuba at 2*shorter<=longer;
  Karatsuba at shorter<=256; otherwise Toom-3. num-bigint strips low zero limbs
  before that full-product schedule and has separate zero/scalar exits.
  Two 40-limb powers of the word base classify as Karatsuba locally but execute
  the backend basecase after trimming to one limb. Adding low one digits to
  both operands retains 40 limbs and reaches Karatsuba. A local label therefore
  is not proof of the selected backend kernel.
- Division computes divisor width, then checks dividend<divisor, zero dividend
  and equality before the width branch. Backend div_rem checks a one-limb
  divisor earlier, and borrowed remainder has a u32-divisor shortcut. For 2/3,
  the local tag is trivial/small but backend division and remainder execute
  single-limb routines. Classification does not validate a nonzero divisor:
  0/0 is labeled trivial and positive/0 single-limb.
- Radix classification uses 32 native-word limbs, while locked non-power-of-two
  conversion uses its large-base path at 64. The 32..63 range is mislabeled.
  The helper takes no radix and does not represent zero/power-of-two shortcuts.
  Current callers submit labels before rational decimal formatting; the event
  does not observe conversion or validate output.
- The remainder wrapper submits its label before computing the exact borrowed
  BigUint remainder; zero-divisor panic can occur after recording an event.
  Valid output is in [0,divisor), with rational sign/normalization handled by
  its consumer. No total-resource or cancellation contract is added. Trace
  classifier arguments are evaluated before the recorder's active-scope check,
  even when recording is inactive but the feature is compiled.
- Native-word counting agrees with the locked digit configuration on 32/64-bit
  pointer targets, includes low zero limbs, and is not an allocation metric.
  The runtime reproductions here are on the current 64-bit host, not a separate
  32-bit platform qualification.

## Hyperreal rational-comparison documentation batch

Reviewed every line of the 331-line baseline
crates/hyperreal/src/rational/arithmetic/comparison.rs at a436077a3.
The final file has 489 lines. Review covered every equality/order/hash branch,
leading-significand bound, local constant, iterator state transition, field and
trait implementation. Context reads covered retained dyadic facts, internal
unreduced storage and canonicalization, binary-magnitude and finite-float
consumers, the checked word-product kernel, Real's immediate-equality consumer,
and relevant tests. These bounded context reads confer no whole-file credit on
larger consumer or test files.

The owning layer is Hyperreal exact rational comparison and its borrowed
magnitude filters. Relevant properties are P1/P3 (exact answers and honest
incomplete evidence), P4/P10 (fact-cache effects and ordered shortcuts), P5/P6
(resource and private-helper preconditions), and the Rustdoc mandate. The domain
is valid rational storage, including correctly marked internal unreduced
fractions; helper restrictions are stated separately. Missing acceptance was
accurate documentation of every private item, the actual cheap-proof order,
normalization meaning, cache effects and input/resource limits. Before editing,
the 29 selected all-feature tests passed on the target revision.

Added or replaced 28 documentation blocks: seven impls, twelve functions/methods,
two function-local constants, one struct, five fields and one associated type.
Documented default equality/ordering methods and iterator behavior supplied by
standard traits; there are no derives or generated item definitions in this
fragment. No noncomment token, branch order, trace event, assertion, feature gate
or runtime operation changed. No hidden item or lint suppression was introduced.

Reviewed mathematical and practical contracts:

- Equality is exact value equality. Its incomplete immediate helper tries
  allocation identity, signs, stored denominator equality, dyadic recognition,
  checked word products and binary magnitudes in order. Equal unavailable
  magnitude results mean unresolved evidence, not inequality. General equality
  lazily cross-multiplies if necessary. Ordering also uses strict leading-bound
  separation before its cross-product fallback and reverses magnitude order
  for negative values. Zero/sign invariants belong to valid stored fractions.
- Hashing canonicalizes an internal unreduced fraction through the reserved
  shared product-cache slot and hashes sign, reduced numerator and denominator.
  Comparisons do not require reduction, but dyadic recognition can learn facts.
  Hash input equality is not a stable serialization or checksum guarantee.
- Integer significand bounds represent value/2^(bits-1) with integer endpoints
  over 2^52. At most 53 bits gives coincident endpoints; wider inputs use the
  leading 53 bits and its successor, even with an all-zero discarded tail.
  Strict order uses products at most 2^107, fitting u128. Overlap/equality is
  unresolved. The float helper encloses abs(value)/2^msd; its caller may supply
  the raw bit-count difference rather than the exact floor-log2. Endpoint
  conversion and scaling by one/two are exact in that normalized range;
  adjacent outward floats account for division rounding. The exact fraction
  remains authoritative.
- The shifted comparator requires positive integers and nonoverflowing u64
  width sums. Reproduced outside that domain: comparing zero shifted by 65
  against one returns Greater; one shifted by u64::MAX panics with overflow
  checks and returns Less without them. These are documented private-helper
  limitations, not demonstrated public rational regressions. Current eligible
  rational comparison/magnitude paths establish positivity; canonical zeros
  exit earlier and marked unreduced fractions bypass the dyadic helper.
- The iterator itself accepts zero but emits shift/64 zero words, so that
  stream is not a canonical integer word representation. A residual shift
  avoids shifting by 64 through lazy initialization, and a nonzero high spill
  precedes adjacent-word windows. Equal positive shifted widths justify equal
  stream lengths. Borrowing avoids full shifted integers but does not bound
  total scan work. Neither arbitrary-width fallback nor hashing has a local
  work/memory/cancellation budget or typed exhaustion result.

Executed after the final edit:

- Locked/offline focused library tests pass: 28 without default features and
  29 with all features. Filters cover comparison, equality, unreduced hashing,
  strict leading-significand order, generated significand bounds, exact msd,
  magnitude thresholds and finite-float enclosures. This includes Real and
  Computable consumers selected by those filters. Existing dyadic dispatch
  count and retained-fact assertions remain unchanged and pass. This is not a
  claim that the entire crate, downstream matrix or workflow suite was run.
- Private cargo doc --lib --no-deps --document-private-items passes in both
  feature configurations, denying warnings and broken/private intra-doc links.
  The all-feature HTML inventory verifies all 26 normally rendered descriptions
  and their applicable anchors, plus inherited comparison/iterator anchors.
  Rustdoc omits function-local constants; a supplemental fixture lifts only
  those two unchanged declarations/comments to module scope and renders both.
  This fixture does not assert that normal Rustdoc includes local items.
- Isolated probes extract the unchanged helper bodies from baseline and final
  source, hosting numerator/denominator fields locally for interval helpers.
  They are not replacement integrated Rational implementations. Both overflow
  modes give byte-identical before/after records within each mode: 55 integer
  enclosures, 605 word streams, 3,080 float interval attempts, 252 interval
  orders and two invalid-domain observations (3,994 records). Each run also
  checks 18,468 positive shifted comparisons against materialized shifts.
- Independent Python integer/Fraction checks verify all integer bounds and
  reconstructed streams, scale eligibility and exact rational containment for
  float intervals, and every decided interval order. The 3,080 attempts include
  expected None outcomes; they are not all successful enclosures. Built-in
  generated tests additionally retain their original 10,000 significand and
  5,000 comparison corpora. Before/after equality alone is not the correctness
  oracle, and these finite checks are not a universal proof.
- Declaration/rendered-description inventory, noncomment-token equality and
  git diff --check pass. Full workflow/format/performance checks remain waived
  by the repository owner for this docs-only session. No performance or
  existing include-fragment formatting claim is made.

## Hyperreal rational-storage and retention documentation batch

Reviewed every line of four files at 24b1ba62e: rational/arithmetic/
representation.rs (391 baseline lines), as_ref.rs (6), retention_tests.rs (145),
and rational/arithmetic.rs (30), all under crates/hyperreal/src/. Final lengths
are 672, 8, 171 and 40 lines respectively. This covers every storage field,
placeholder variant, flag, static pool, atomic operation, trait method, tracing
macro, test helper and facade declaration in those files. Context reads covered
canonicalization and small-value construction, binary/unary cache installation
and lookup, unique owned negation, square extraction/power admission, conversion
facts, the trace recorder/classifiers, relevant tests and the root export list.
Those bounded reads do not grant whole-file credit to the larger consumers.

The owning layer is Hyperreal rational representation and retained exact
arithmetic evidence. Relevant properties are P1/P3 (exact storage and truthful
facts), P4/P10 (identity, publication, invalidation and dispatch), P5/P6 (resource
and failure limits), and private/generated Rustdoc coverage. The domain includes
valid reduced and explicitly marked internal unreduced fractions, canonical
zero, weak/strong cache identities, finite conversions and Serde wire records.
Missing acceptance was documentation of all private items, actual cache roles,
atomic semantics, input normalization and resource scope. Before edits, all
37 selected all-feature test executions passed. The existing single-bit
observation comment was inaccurate: fetch-or cannot give two racing observers
the initially clear state without a reset.

Added or replaced 123 authored documentation blocks: 114 in representation,
two in AsRef, five in retention tests and two in the facade. The representation
inventory includes eight structs (one function-local), two enums, eleven variants,
27 named/tuple fields, ten impls, seventeen methods, one associated type,
nineteen constants, thirteen statics and six macros. Tuple fields now have
individual descriptions without changing their syntax tokens or layout.
Removed the pre-existing doc(hidden) from RationalData. No noncomment token
changed apart from that documentation attribute; no visibility, algorithm,
branch, synchronization ordering, assertion or feature gate changed.

Reviewed and reproduced contracts:

- Rational clones share exact storage, caches and facts. AsRef borrows the same
  handle; Deref borrows the payload without canonicalization. Debug and Serde
  serialization obtain canonical parts and omit caches. RationalData has public
  visibility as the trait target but no direct root re-export; a downstream
  caller can name it as <Rational as Deref>::Target. Its fields remain private.
- CompactOnceBox represents empty by null, publishes a fully constructed box
  with release/acquire ordering, returns a losing publisher's box, and clears
  only through exclusive access. Clear nulls the pointer before dropping, can
  be followed by another publication, and destruction drops the installed box.
  Its explicit Sync implementation requires T: Send + Sync; field auto traits
  govern Send. Fixed slot storage does not bound T's allocation or destructor.
- Product entries use weak other-operand identity and strong exact results;
  the unreduced marker instead reserves that slot for canonicalization.
  Linear tags encode product/sum/two difference directions, strong/weak inverse
  and negation links, and a square-layout placeholder. Inert zeros in placeholder
  records are not arithmetic answers. Weak keys preserve allocation identity
  without keeping the operand value alive. Consumer schedules retain two binary
  entries plus eligible unary links and an independent square-reduction pair.
  Slot count is bounded; retained values/graphs and temporary racing work are not.
- Learned bits use relaxed operations because they do not publish cache payloads.
  retained_fact and observe_retained_fact test any mask overlap, not all bits;
  a zero mask returns false. Exactly one racing single-bit fetch-or sees false
  before a reset. Exclusive owned negation clears reuse observations/caches while
  retaining applicable magnitude facts. Packed dyadic exponents use bits 8..30
  for exponent+1, so the largest encoded exponent is 2^23-2; this is not a bound
  on admitted rational denominators.
- Static intern pools have process lifetime and no eviction/reset: integers
  2..=64 per sign; 32 odd dyadic numerators through 63 at shifts 1..=63 (2,016
  slots per sign); and the 63 by 63 general-fraction grid (3,969 slots per sign),
  with ineligible combinations unpopulated. Retained arithmetic graphs can grow
  beyond the small values themselves. The integer constants and pool indices
  were checked against their actual consumers.
- Serde rejects a zero denominator before zero/sign normalization. NoSign with a
  nonzero numerator and signed zero numerators normalize to zero; they are not
  all rejected. Nonzero fractions reduce exactly. Derived wire decoding accepts
  supported map/sequence forms, ignores unknown map fields by default, and
  rejects missing/duplicate known fields and malformed component values. Replay
  restores value, not arbitrary allocation identity or cached evidence, and has
  no local work/byte budget. This does not promise compatibility across every
  possible Serde format's struct-name conventions.
- Tracing macros compile away with their arguments when disabled. When enabled,
  argument evaluation precedes the recording-scope check. Temporary events can
  include interned clones and are not allocation counts. Reduction/GCD/factor
  events trust supplied observations; backend division/radix labels classify
  operands rather than observe actual backend execution, as recorded in the
  earlier diagnostic batch.

## Hyperreal rational-formatting and parsing documentation batch

Reviewed every line of the 460-line baseline
crates/hyperreal/src/rational/arithmetic/format_parse.rs at 5b1b902b1.
The final file has 636 lines. Review covered Display's flags and streaming
writes, all decimal/scientific helpers, power-cache recursion, the FromStr
branch order and typed errors. Context included the already documented parse
anchor, rational canonicalization/construction, Problem variants, the locked
num-bigint 0.4.6 radix parser, Real parsing tests and existing rational parser/
format/trace tests. These context reads do not give the larger files new
whole-file review credit.

The owning layer is Hyperreal's exact rational text boundary. Relevant properties
are P1/P3 (exact values and honest presentation/grammar claims), P4/P10 (preserved
canonicalization/dispatch order), P5/P6 (checked amplification and failure scope),
and Rustdoc coverage. The intended exact input domain is ASCII digit-only signed
integers, fractions, decimals and scientific literals; actual fallback acceptance
and its defects are recorded separately. Missing acceptance was documentation of
every helper, the difference between display and replay, the true resource guard,
and backend syntax interactions. Before editing, all eleven selected rational
parser/formatter/trace tests passed, and the additional public probe reproduced
the syntax inconsistencies below. The initial Real filter matched zero tests;
it was replaced with the actual five-test path for final downstream validation.

Added sixteen blocks: three impls, ten functions, two constants and one associated
error type. Every authored item is documented and rendered; this fragment has no
local or generated type/macro definitions needing supplemental rendering.
Two runnable examples demonstrate exact parsing, typed failures, mixed display
and truncation. No noncomment token, dispatch event/order, constant, branch,
assertion, cache operation or feature gate changed. No hidden item or suppression
was introduced. Existing include-fragment formatting is preserved.

Reviewed and reproduced behavior:

- Default Display canonicalizes marked unreduced parts and emits an integer,
  proper fraction or mixed fraction. The sign applies to the whole value.
  Mixed output such as 1 2/3 fails FromStr with BadFraction, so Display is not a
  general native replay format. Alternate noninteger output performs exact
  long division but truncates toward zero, with default maximum 1,000 fractional
  digits. It stops at a zero remainder without trailing-zero padding; precision
  zero still writes the point. Integers use integral padding and ignore precision/
  alternate. Nonintegers honor plus but ignore width/alignment/zero padding.
  Sink errors propagate; output precision is not a total-work or memory budget.
- FromStr strips at most one sign, then dispatches scientific before slash before
  point before integer. That branch determines BadDecimal/BadFraction/BadInteger.
  Both 1/0 and 0/0 give DivideByZero. Decimal/scientific values use exact powers
  of ten, never a float import. Ordinary integer/fraction/decimal inputs have no
  source-length guard matching the scientific amplification check.
- Checked u128 helpers require ASCII digits, accept arbitrarily many leading
  zeros, and stop on malformed input or overflow. Exponent validation instead
  continues scanning after usize overflow: a later nondigit remains BadDecimal;
  a valid overflowing exponent is represented separately as None. A fully
  validated zero significand returns zero even with an enormous exponent.
- Scientific scale arithmetic cancels exponent, fractional length and stripped
  trailing zeros, but checked additions occur before cancellation. Overflow of
  those intermediate sums gives Exhausted. The inclusive power allowance is
  source significand bytes plus one million, with saturating addition. It is
  checked before and after trailing-zero removal; this is an amplification
  guard, not an allocator/work/cancellation contract. The private sign argument
  is Plus or Minus. Wide denominator construction cancels binary factors for
  even final digits, recognizes odd non-five coprimality, and otherwise reduces.
- Magnitude parsing first tries u128, then backend parsing below 8,192 bytes,
  then the local product tree. Long all-zero inputs can stay on the word path.
  Tree leaves are shorter than 4,096 bytes. The exact digit-only recurrence is
  left*10^(right length)+right. Its BTreeMap keys are right byte lengths and
  callers must supply correct 10^key entries. Hits clone their BigUint; failed
  recursion can leave valid earlier entries in the map. The ordinary entry point
  starts with a fresh map. Historical crossover comments were read as provenance,
  not reproduced as a current performance claim.

Reproduced implementation gaps, not repaired or redefined as exact support:

- The locked BigUint leaf parser accepts a leading plus and underscores after
  an initial digit. Word and scientific paths reject those bytes. Consequently
  ++1 becomes 1, -+1 becomes -1, and 1/+2 becomes 1/2 through fallback paths.
  Whitespace and mixed fractions remain rejected.
- Fallback fractional length counts separator/sign bytes even though the leaf
  parser ignores/consumes them: 1.2_5 becomes 41/40, .+5 becomes 1/20 and 1.+5
  becomes 21/20. The scientific versions with those extra bytes are rejected.
- For source `1` + `0` repeated (L-2) times + `_`, lengths 4,095, 4,096 and
  8,191 produce 10^(L-2), matching separator removal. At L=8,192, 8,193 and
  10,240 the tree instead produces 10^(L-1). An 8,192-byte string of ones with
  byte 4,096 replaced by underscore is rejected as BadInteger because a leaf
  begins with underscore, despite whole-input backend acceptance. These original
  witnesses and adjacent pure-digit controls are preserved in probe scripts.
- A deliberately false prefilled tree power produces a false result, confirming
  the private helper's trusted-cache precondition; this is not a public cache
  poisoning path, because the normal entry creates its own map. A separate bad
  trailing-character fixture returns None while retaining the earlier valid
  10^2048 entry. These are distinct from the public separator-scaling defects.

Executed after the final source edit:

- Locked/offline focused tests pass: fourteen without default features and
  sixteen with all features, including five Real parser consumers. Existing
  exact-value, reduced-part, hash and dispatch count assertions are unchanged.
  Both added doctests pass in each configuration. The baseline subset had eleven
  passing all-feature tests; no zero-match filter is counted as acceptance.
- Private cargo doc --lib --no-deps --document-private-items passes in both
  configurations with warnings and broken/private intra-doc links denied.
  All sixteen complete descriptions and applicable method/constant/trait anchors
  are checked in the all-feature HTML. No universal coverage inference is made
  from successful doc compilation alone.
- Public baseline/final probes give eighty byte-identical complete records:
  68 parse outcomes and twelve formatting rows (eleven formats each), including
  full dispatch snapshots. Six failing-sink attempts propagate fmt::Error.
  The large pure-digit controls span 4,095 through 10,240 bytes, with separator
  cases alongside them and validated zero with a huge exponent.
- Extracted unchanged helper bodies give 234 byte-identical before/after records:
  fourteen word cases (including u128 boundaries and 10,000 leading zeros),
  twelve exponent cases, 160 checked net-power cases, forty amplification-boundary
  cases, six tree/cache records, one failed tree and one invalid-cache fixture.
  Word/parts equivalence is also checked at every UTF-8 boundary split of the

- Independent Python integers/Fraction expectations check the 234 helper records,
  all 68 public parse values/errors and all 132 formatted strings. Pure-digit

  presentation is checked by exact scaled integer division and denominator

- Noncomment-token equality, authored-item/rendered-description inventory and
  git diff --check pass. Full workflow/format/performance checks remain waived
